name: Hide of the Cunning Hunter
summary: One of the first Charms young Lunars learn; suppresses the Lunar's Tell, making it effectively invisible under most circumstances.
description: The effects of this Charm dissipate if the Lunar's anima banner reaches or exceeds the 4-7 motes level of display. Otherwise, it's impossible to detect the Lunar's tattoos/Tell, even for forms of sight that would perceive the effects of active Essence. Storytellers should assume individuals who see a Lunar with unsuppressed tattoos will regard the Lunar suspiciously for the purposes of perceiving his Tell, and most will immediately realize the character's nature.

name: Masking the Brilliant Form
summary: Extends Tell-suppression so it works even while the Lunar's anima is active and blazing at the 4-7 motes display level.
description: While active, it is impossible to perceive the Tell of a Lunar who has never purchased Deadly Beastman Transformation. Lunars who have purchased Deadly Beastman Transformation 1-2 times are treated as if they had never purchased it for the purposes of having their Tells spotted. Lunars who have purchased Deadly Beastman Transformation 3+ times are treated as if they purchased it 1-2 times for the purposes of Tell-spotting. Effects end when the character's anima becomes more intense than the 4-7 motes level.

name: Finding the Spirit's Shape
summary: The Lunar chooses an animal no larger than an elk and no smaller than a large cat; that animal becomes her totem/spirit animal and its shape becomes a second true form.
description: Reflexive; almost all Lunars know this Charm. A Lunar either tastes the heart's blood of her totem animal during initiation, or in many cases, finds the totem-shape when she Exalts. Such Exalts are driven by an incredible craving to consume the life of a beast of that species so they can fairly gain its form. If a Lunar wants a totem animal larger than a cat, she may fairly know it already; if smaller, she must know it before she can drink its blood to gain the shape. A Lunar may change her totem animal, but doing so is costly and dangerous: she must pay a dot of permanent Willpower and buy the Charm again. Traces of the previous totem form remain in the Lunar's Tell. A Lunar whose Tell combines the traits of several animals is a chimera and is regarded with scorn; in addition, the Lunar may offend the animal avatar of the species she forsakes.

name: Deadly Beastman Transformation
summary: Shifts the Lunar into a monstrous human/totem-animal hybrid war-form, three feet taller than her normal height, mistakable for nothing but a sleek and deadly killing machine.
description: This hybrid shape is one of the Lunar's true forms and includes many bonuses. The first time a character takes this Charm, she receives five Attribute points and two gifts, applied immediately after purchase; subsequent purchases each grant three Attribute points and one gift. A character can purchase this Charm no more times than she has points of Essence. Each Attribute point raises Strength or Stamina by 1, or two points raise Dexterity by 1; bonuses are fixed once allocated and cannot be saved up between purchases or moved later. These bonus Attributes count as natural Attributes for the purposes of Charms that double Attributes and of Charms that convert Attribute dice to automatic successes. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.

name: Calling Luna's Favor
summary: Lets the Lunar manifest one of her Deadly Beastman Transformation gifts while still in human or totem (non-hybrid) form.
description: From immediately after activation until the end of the scene or until the character ends the Charm's effects, the Lunar enjoys the benefits of one of her Deadly Beastman Transformation gifts. The gift actually manifests and is an obvious mark of a supernatural character; it manifests regardless of whether or not it has prerequisite gifts.

name: Blossoming Gift of Luna
summary: Extension of Calling Luna's Favor that lets the Lunar retain a single manifested gift indefinitely, rather than only for a scene.
description: By activating this Charm while in Beastman form, the Lunar may retain a single Deadly Beastman Transformation gift until she ends the Charm's effects or next enters hybrid form. As with Calling Luna's Favor, the gift actually manifests and is in no way concealed; it manifests regardless of whether the gift has prerequisites.

name: Towering Beast Form
summary: Knowledge-only Charm (no activation cost) that enhances the Lunar's hybrid war-form, letting it scale up to as large as a Tyrant Lizard or other large dinosaur, rather than being capped at elk-size.
description: There is no cost to use this Charm's effects — simply learning it enhances the Lunar's capabilities passively. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.

name: Humble Mouse Shape
summary: Knowledge-only Charm that lets the Lunar shapeshift into forms smaller than a cat, down to as small as a field mouse.
description: There is no cost to use this Charm's effects — learning it simply enhances the Lunar's capabilities. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.

name: Shaping the Ideal Form
summary: Lets the Lunar make cosmetic changes to the appearance of any of her true forms.
description: Modifications include changing hair, eye, or skin color by several shades, lengthening or shortening hair length, and reshaping a chin or nose slightly or straightening teeth. A modification only applies to the form in which it was used — altering hair color in both human and totem-animal shapes requires using the Charm twice. Shaping the Ideal Form does not allow the Lunar to assume the appearance of another being, though it may help disguise his appearance; Lunars who wish to assume the form of specific individuals must instead use the Charm Prey's Skin Disguise. Shaping the Ideal Form cannot be used to conceal the Lunar's Tell or tattoos. No matter how much effort is put into the shaping, the Charm cannot be used to improve the Lunar's Physical Attributes unless the player invests experience in raising the Attribute — in that case, training time can represent an extended campaign of cosmetic self-improvement by reshaping. Overuse of the Charm tends to detract from the Lunar's appearance, rendering him bland, and is regarded as a sign of degeneracy and vanity among Luna's Beloved.

name: Many-Faced Moon Transformation
summary: Changes the gender the Exalt presents through any of her true forms.
description: Males become females and vice versa through their personalities, knowledge, and Traits unchanged. This is not a cosmetic modification — the Charm changes the Lunar's biology, and he or she becomes capable of siring or bearing children in either sex. While many Lunars have a preferred gender, individual Lunars have a 'natural' sex — they're considered to be in true form in either gender. Attempts by a pregnant Lunar to use this Charm automatically fail. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.

name: Prey's Skin Disguise
summary: Lets the Lunar assume the outward appearance of a specific other human she has consumed.
description: The Lunar must consume the target's heart's blood to gain this appearance. She gains the victim's outward appearance and Physical Attributes and Appearance, but not the victim's knowledge, Mental or Social Attributes, or Abilities. If the target is an Exalt, the Lunar gains his outward appearance but remains a Lunar. This Charm cannot be used to mimic the Fair Folk, who, though humanoid, are something other. The character can still dress and act any way she desires — she adopts the victim's outward appearance, not personality. A Lunar willing to consume many mortals can develop quite a diverse catalog of shapes. As with any other type of shapechanging, the appearance of the character's Tell and tattoos is unchanged. Lunars who wish to masquerade as the persons they consumed would thus be well-advised to use Charms to suppress those unmistakable signs. Members of the Eclipse Caste may not learn this Charm, for it draws on a natural power of the Lunar Exalted that Solars cannot master or emulate.
prerequisiteText: Towering Beast Form, Humble Mouse Shape, Many-Faced Moon Transformation

name: Lunar Blood Reshaping Technique
summary: By having a willing subject taste the Lunar's blood, the Lunar can make minor alterations to that subject's form.
description: The range of possible changes are as per Shaping the Ideal Form — this Charm cannot be used to change a target's shape to a specific person's or to give her the appearance of another human. Unlike modifications the Lunar makes to himself, the changes fade after a day. The subject must also spend a temporary Willpower point (two if she is an Exalt). Unwilling subjects, tattooed Lunars, non-humans, the undead, and unmaterialized spirits cannot be shaped by this Charm. Once the Charm is activated, the player rolls Manipulation + Craft (Body Shaping) at standard difficulty. One success or more indicates success, while if the roll fails, the subject's form is unaltered. A botch, however, results in an unexpected — and usually unpleasant — outcome.

name: Wondrous Lunar Transformation
summary: A more powerful version of the Lunar Blood Reshaping Technique, allowing the Lunar to alter a subject's form to match one of the patterns in the Lunar's 'library.'
description: This process is difficult and painful for the subject and requires immense skill by the Lunar, but it allows the subject to attain a non-human form or to masquerade as another human. In addition to the costs to the Lunar, the subject must spend 2 temporary Willpower points (3 if an Exalt). Unwilling subjects, tattooed Lunars, non-humans, the undead, and unmaterialized spirits cannot be shaped by this Charm. Once the Charm is activated, the Lunar's player rolls Manipulation + Craft (Body Shaping) at difficulty 3. Three or more successes indicates success, while if the roll fails (or gets only one or two successes), the subject's form is unaltered. A botch, however, results in an unexpected — and usually unpleasant — outcome, probably a subject twisted and crippled for the duration or possibly suffering permanent damage.
prerequisiteText: Prey's Skin Disguise, Lunar Blood Reshaping Technique

name: Shaping the Once-Living Form
summary: Lets the Lunar reshape inert, once-living material (wood, bone) into another form — a weapon, a piece of armor, or clothing.
description: The Lunar cannot use this Charm to create complex objects with moving parts (a simple buckle is about as sophisticated as it gets), nor can it be used to reshape objects that are already under the influence of Charms, sorcery, or other supernatural effects. The item to be shaped must be smeared with the Lunar's blood, costing him a single health level (unsoakable lethal damage) before Essence can be channeled into the object. The texture and appearance of the original material remains unaltered (a wood weapon is always still wood, not metal), though the product may be modified by conventional means (dyes, paint, and so forth). The Essence cost of the Charm reflects the amount of raw material affected. If the target object is roughly the same size as the raw material, the Essence cost of the Charm is unaltered. If a size change is part of the process, the Lunar must spend additional Essence motes allowing the final product's size to be twice (or half) that of the raw material. An object fashioned in this manner is not permanent, but rather remains the Lunar commits the Essence. If the Lunar uses the Essence for other purposes, the product reverts to original form. A Lunar can, however, make his construct permanent by spending a point of Willpower, but he may only do so at the moment of creation. In this case, the Charm is instant, and the Essence returns normally. Shaping the object requires a Manipulation + Craft roll, usually of difficulty 1. The Storyteller may, however, increase this difficulty for more complex shapes. This Charm cannot effect the undead.
cost: 1 mote per raw cubic foot, 1 per volume increase + 1 health level

name: Fish Tail Technique
summary: Transforms the Lunar's limbs to enhance swimming: turning limbs into flippers, webbing hands and feet, or similar effects.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar transforms his limbs to enhance his swimming abilities, turning his limbs into flippers, webbing hands and feet or performing other similar effects (at the Lunar's discretion) to enhance his swimming abilities, allowing him to move through water unimpeded at twice his normal movement rate. If he is in a form with innate swimming abilities, such as if a shark or a seal, this Charm confers no additional benefits. This Charm does not confer the ability to breathe water, and the character must surface to breathe (per the holding breath rules on p. 243 of Exalted) or risk drowning.

name: Tool-Hand Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar reshape her hands and fingers into the shapes of tools for craft tasks, without needing prefabricated tools.
description: Most Lunars abhor the trappings of civilization, but this does not mean that they don't occasionally require tools. Unlike mortals, who must keep a range of prefabricated tools for such circumstances, a Lunar can reshape his body to provide the necessary instruments. Hands are strengthened and fingers and claws sharpened and reshaped to provide any tool the Exalt might need. While using the Tool-Hand Technique, the Lunar can naturally perform tasks that would normally require tools (for example, boring a hole in wood, hammering a peg or picking at stone). The Lunar's hands, feet or whatever else is shaped into the tool takes on a superficial resemblance to the tool in question but remains indisputably flesh and bone (albeit flesh and bone surrounded by a nimbus of Essence). A Lunar with multiple limbs can equip multiple limbs at a cost of 1 mote per limb and suffers no injury from the pounding, cutting or rasping of using the 'tools.' The Tool-Hand Technique cannot be used to form weapons or to otherwise give the Lunar an advantage in inflicting or withstanding damage, nor does the Lunar work faster than she would with normal tools. Any rolls involving Craft gain +2 dice when the Lunar uses this Charm.

name: Rat-Head Technique
summary: Deforms the Lunar's bones, muscles, and organs to squeeze through gaps far too small to normally fit through.
description: By means of this Charm, the Lunar can squeeze his bones, muscles and organs capable of immense deformation, allowing him to squeeze through gaps it would not normally fit. By means of this Charm, a human-sized Lunar could wriggle through a hole as small as a mouse hole or a knothole in a fence. The process is very unsettling to watch and is likewise uncomfortable for the Lunar. The Rat-Head Technique cannot be used as part of any Combo or while the Lunar is under the effects of a Charm or sorcery that hardens or reinforces his limbs in any manner (such as the Body Weapon Technique). While using this Charm, the Lunar's natural soak cannot exceed 2B/2L under any circumstances, and he cannot parry lethal attacks without an appropriate stunt — his 'softened' body lacks the strength to do so effectively. A Lunar under the effect of Rat-Head Technique may dodge normally.

name: Ox-Body Technique
summary: Lets the Lunar buy extra health levels as if it were a Charm, purchasable once per dot of human-form Stamina.
description: The bodies of the Exalted are far more durable than those of mere mortals. To help simulate this, an Exalt may buy extra health levels as if they were a Charm. A player may purchase this Charm up to once per dot of human-form Stamina his character possesses. Each Ox-Body Technique Charm purchased can provide two -1 health levels or four -2 health levels, at the player's option, determined at the time of purchase.
reviewFlags: Source lists this Charm’s requirement as "Minimum Stamina: varies" (purchasable multiple times, scaling with Stamina) rather than a single fixed rating; simplified to a baseline Stamina 1 minimum, matching the existing Solar/Abyssal/Sidereal Ox-Body Technique catalog entries’ own precedent for the same Charm name.

name: Crouching Tiger Exercise
summary: A preparation ritual that lets the Lunar temporarily boost his Strength.
description: Lunars employ Essence to enhance their muscles via this Charm, using a series of stances and static exercises to focus Essence into their limbs, increasing their strength and resilience. A Lunar using this Charm swells into an intimidating, muscular brute. Her tendons stand out like taut rope, and her muscles seem ready to burst through her skin. The Exalt's player makes a Strength + Athletics roll. For every success, add one to the Lunar's Strength. That character cannot more than double her initial Strength through the use of this Charm. This is a dice bonus added by a Charm and should be considered as such when determining the maximum effect of other dice-bonus Charms. The Charm's effects last for a number of turns equal to the character's Essence + the number of success rolled. The exercises used to activate the Crouching Tiger Exercise require the character's undivided dice action for a number of turns equal to 10 + (the Lunar's Strength prior to the performance of this exercise). These turns of preparation must be concurrent and uninterrupted and cannot be combined with the preparation periods of other, similar exercises.

name: Moonsilver Monkey Exercise
summary: A preparation ritual, parallel to the Crouching Tiger Exercise, that lets the Lunar temporarily boost his Dexterity.
description: By performing a series of limbering-up exercises and stances as he directs Essence through his muscles, a Lunar Exalt can temporarily boost his hand-eye coordination, his movements becoming fluid and graceful as moonsilver. The Exalted's player makes a Dexterity + Athletics roll. For every success, add one to the Lunar's Dexterity. That character cannot more than double his initial Dexterity through the use of this Charm. This is a dice bonus added by a Charm and should be considered as such when determining the maximum effect of other dice-bonus Charms. The Charm's effects last for a number of turns equal to the character's Essence + the number of success rolled. Enacting the Moonsilver Monkey Exercise requires the character's undivided action for a number of turns equal to (the Lunar's Dexterity prior to the performance of this exercise) + 10. These turns of preparation must be concurrent and uninterrupted, and cannot be combined with the preparation periods of other, similar exercises.

name: Regaining Breath Exercise
summary: Lets the Lunar draw on his strength of spirit to fortify and regain Essence.
description: In addition to using his Essence to fortify his body, a Lunar can draw on his strength of spirit to fortify Essence. By entering a trance and focusing his mind inward for a number of turns equal to (20 - his Stamina), a Lunar can regain motes of Essence via a Stamina + Endurance roll. For every success, the Lunar regains 2 motes of Essence. The character cannot regain more than his normal maximum temporary Essence, nor can he regain more than (his permanent Essence x 2) motes per use of the Charm. These turns of concentration must be concurrent and uninterrupted and cannot be combined with the preparation periods of other, similar exercises.
prerequisiteText: Crouching Tiger Exercise, Moonsilver Monkey Exercise

name: Breath-Drinking Executioner Attack
summary: Lets the Lunar trap and consume the vital energy released by a slain individual to restore her own Essence reserves.
description: The death of an individual releases the target's lower or 'animal' soul, from which the Lunar can trap and consume vital energy to restore her Essence reserves. By means of the Breath-Drinking Executioner Attack, a Lunar can trap and consume this vital energy to restore her Essence reserves. By activating the Charm immediately after slaying an opponent, a Lunar regains the result of one 10-sided die in motes of Essence. An Exalt cannot regain more Essence in a given turn than she has points of Stamina.

name: Predator Grace Method
summary: Grants the Lunar premature balance beyond even the greatest feline.
description: The Exalt can walk across surfaces as fragile as bamboo and string with ease and easily resists efforts to unbalance him. By spending motes of Essence, the Lunar's player may convert Dexterity dice into automatic successes when making a single Athletics roll to resist or resist balance and climbing or resist sweeps, clinches, holds or tackles. Upon activating the Charm, the Lunar's body and features undergo subtle changes, resulting in a lithe and graceful appearance that shifts to give him the best balance and grip possible in the present circumstances. The Lunar may not exceed his normal maximum temporary Essence through the use of this Charm.

name: Panther Stride Stance
summary: The Lunar's legs shift into the likeness of the legs of a giant cat, greatly increasing running and leaping speed for a scene.
description: Using this Charm, the Lunar's legs shift into the likeness of the legs of a giant cat, and his whole body twists, slightly becoming lower and more streamlined. For the remainder of the scene, the Lunar can move at twice his normal movement rate and leap three times his normal jumping distance. If the target surface is uncertain, the Lunar's player must still make a (Dexterity or Wits) + Athletics roll to land successfully after such a leap (see p. 252 of Exalted). A Lunar may carry a 'passenger' on such a leap, doing so reduces his effective Dexterity by one and his effective Strength by two. A Full Moon who uses this Charm in conjunction with his anima power moves at three times his normal movement rate and leaps five times his normal jumping distance.

name: Cat-Falling Attitude
summary: Greatly improves the Lunar's ability to avoid damage from a fall.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar greatly improves his ability to avoid damage from a fall. He will always land on his feet and suffers only one level of bashing damage for every 10 feet fallen. Furthermore, he only suffers lethal damage if he falls more than 100 feet or onto a treacherous surface such as spikes.

name: Flying Tiger Technique
summary: Creates a flap of skin between the Lunar's arms and legs, drastically extending her leaping ability into gliding.
description: By creating a flap of skin between his arms and legs, a Lunar can drastically extend his leaping abilities. Using the skin flap as crude gliding wings, a Lunar using this technique can extend his horizontal leaping distance in excess of 10 times his normal leaping distance, though this depends on his trading height for distance. He can travel 20 yards per dot of Strength and Athletics, and another two yards for every yard of altitude he descends. For example, a Lunar with Strength 3, Athletics 3 who leaps from a branch 100 yards up may glide to a point on the ground 320 yards away ([3 x 20] + [3 x 20] + [2 x 100] yards). The Lunar may attempt to extend this distance by rolling Dexterity + Athletics, each success adding 10 percent to the range. The anima powers of a Full Moon Lunar and other movement-enhancing Charms do not add to the gliding distance of the Skin-Flap Flying Method.

name: Tree-Dwelling Jaguar Claws
summary: Lets the Lunar grow and adapt claws to grip trees (or other surfaces where claws can grip) with surprising ease.
description: Using his protean abilities to grow claws and to adapt his skeleton and muscles, a Lunar Exalted can ascend trees (or other surfaces where his claws can grip) with surprising ease. A Lunar normally uses half his movement rate when climbing but may use his full movement rate without penalty if his player makes a successful Dexterity + Athletics roll. When faced with difficult climbing conditions (high winds, overhangs, etc.), a Lunar using this Charm reduces the difficulty of the Dexterity + Athletics rolls by 1 (but not below 1). If the Lunar makes unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attacks while the Charm is active, his attacks inflict lethal damage.

name: Cat Paw Climbing Style
summary: Lets the Lunar ascend, descend, or traverse any surface with relative ease, even if there are no obvious handholds.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar may ascend, descend or traverse any surface with relative ease, even if there are no obvious handholds. Instead, he relies on minute adjustments to his fingers and toes to exploit minute variations in surface texture. The Lunar may move up to half his normal movement rate either horizontally or vertically, and reduces the difficulty of all Dexterity + Athletics rolls by 2 (but not below 1). Lunar characters may carry up to 100 pounds per point of Strength while using this Charm.

name: Body Weapon Technique
summary: Enhances the Lunar's unarmed-combat blows by focusing Essence into his limbs, making an unarmed attack inflict lethal rather than bashing damage.
description: A Lunar may use this Charm to enhance his unarmed-combat abilities, making his blows more deadly by focusing Essence into his limbs. Rather than inflicting bashing damage when executing a single unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack (not a wrestling maneuver), his blow causes lethal damage.

name: Sinuous Striking Grace
summary: Uses Essence flows to suggest the likely actions of allies and enemies, letting the Lunar improve her initiative.
description: The Lunar uses Essence flows to suggest the likely actions of allies and enemies alike. When rolling initiative, the Lunar may spend motes of Essence to improve her initiative rating, 1 mote buying a +1 modifier to a maximum of the Lunar's Dexterity score.

name: Tyrant Lizard Strike
summary: Lets the Lunar instinctively perceive Essence flows in a target, guiding his blows through defenses for incredibly accurate attacks.
description: By means of this Charm, a Lunar can instinctively perceive the flows of Essence in his target, using the Exalt's blows through his victim's defenses, making the claws and teeth incredibly accurate. For each mote of Essence spent on this Charm, the Lunar gains an additional attack die on a single unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. This bonus die may not exceed the character's Dexterity.

name: Snake Body Technique
summary: Lets the Lunar use a civilized enemy's own strength against him by reflecting attacks back before damage is rolled.
description: By utilizing the sinuous movements of a snake, the Lunar can use a civilized enemy's strengths against him. When attacked by a Melee or Martial Arts attack, before damage is rolled, the Exalt's player can make a reflexive Dexterity + Dodge roll against a difficulty equal to the number of successes rolled on the attack. If the roll succeeds, any damage from the attacker is applied to the attacker instead, with extra successes by the Lunar increasing the number of damage dice. Even if the Exalt fails to reflect the attack, the Lunar's successes on the Dexterity + Dodge roll still reduce the attack's successes normally. The Snake Body Technique is a form of dodge and cannot be used against undodgeable attacks, nor can it be used to avoid counterattack-type effects.

name: Coiled Cobra Stance
summary: By holding his body in anticipation of the opponent's actions, the Lunar readies a devastating blow against a foe.
description: The Lunar activates the Charm before rolling initiative and chooses a self-inflicted penalty to that initiative roll. For every point of penalty on the initiative roll, the Lunar gains a bonus die to his attack roll against the foe; this bonus cannot exceed the Exalted's Dexterity, counts against the Exalted's Charm dice, and only applies during turns when the Lunar plans to make Brawl or Martial Arts attacks. If the Lunar does not act in the turn the Charm is activated, the advantages of the Coiled Cobra Stance are lost. If the Lunar fully dodges or aborts to a parry, the effects of the Coiled Cobra Stance are also lost. Coiled Cobra Stance cannot be used in a Combo with Charms that grant extra actions. A character cannot split his dice pool in a turn when he uses the Coiled Cobra Stance.
prerequisiteText: Snake Body Technique, Deadly Viper Strike (from the Unarmed Combat II tree)

name: Hydra Head Attack
summary: Enhances the Lunar's reactions, letting him attack multiple times in a turn.
description: A skilled Lunar can use Essence to enhance his reactions, giving him preternatural reflexes and allowing him to attack multiple times in a turn. For every 3 motes of Essence spent activating this Charm, the Lunar gains an additional unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. The Lunar can buy no more extra actions with permanent Essence, no more than (the character's Essence + 3, rounded down) this Charm normally means (the character's Essence + 3), but Lunars with lower Essence may lose their ability to make extra actions.
reviewFlags: Unarmed Combat I tree. The rendered page's cap-formula wording was awkward/possibly OCR-damaged in the printed original around 'the character's Essence + 3' — re-verify exact wording against the physical page before promotion.

name: Deadly Claw Blow
summary: Lets the Lunar convert Dexterity dice into automatic successes on a single unarmed attack, targeting even dematerialized spirits.
description: This Charm allows the Lunar to harness his bestial prowess to become a killing machine. He becomes instinctively aware of an opponent's weak spots and how to exploit them, allowing him to target his attacks to maximum effect. He may spend Essence to turn his Dexterity dice into automatic successes when making a single unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. The dice converted into automatic successes are not rolled as part of his dice pool but the remaining dice (including Ability dice and any Attribute dice not converted to successes) are rolled normally. Each Attribute die converted costs 2 motes of Essence. The precision of the Deadly Claw Blow allows the Lunar to harm beings not wholly in the material world, allowing him to target spirits even if they are dematerialized.

name: Claws of the Silver Moon
summary: Temporarily transforms the Lunar's claws and fangs into moonsilver, drastically improving her combat abilities.
description: Using this technique, the Lunar temporarily transforms his claws and fangs into moonsilver, drastically improving his combat abilities. When using the Charm, the Lunar may make unarmed claw attacks with his Brawl or Martial Arts at Spd +6, Acc +1, Dmg +3L, Pry +1. He may make unarmed bite attacks with those Abilities at Spd +0, Acc +2, Dmg +5L, Pry +0. Claws of the Silver Moon can harm spirits even if they are dematerialized, and Charms that enhance moonsilver weapons may be used in conjunction with Claws of the Silver Moon.

name: Scimitar Claw Technique
summary: Focuses Essence in the Lunar's claws and teeth, enlarging and reshaping them into vicious rending weapons.
description: Focusing Essence in his claws and teeth, not only does the Lunar transform his claws and teeth into moonsilver, but he also enlarges and reshapes them into vicious rending weapons capable of disemboweling an ill-prepared foe. When using the Charm, the Lunar's claw attacks are Spd +6, Acc +4, Dmg +5L, Pry +4. The Lunar's bite attacks are Spd +3, Acc +2, Dmg +8L, Pry +0. Charms that enhance moonsilver weapons may be used in conjunction with the Scimitar Claw Technique. Claws created with the Scimitar Claw Technique can harm dematerialized spirits.

name: Adder Fang Method
summary: Lets Lunars enhance their attacks with venom by momentarily generating poison glands or ducts.
description: Lunars who know the Adder Fang Method can enhance their attacks with venom. The Charm momentarily creates poison generating glands or ducts, releasing toxins whenever the Lunar successfully makes an unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts bite attack. In addition to the normal damage of the attack, if the target takes damage, she suffers an additional number of dice of lethal damage equal to the Stamina + Essence of the Lunar. This damage is soaked separately and does not add extra successes. However, it ignores the target's armor — only Stamina and other natural soak apply.

name: Burning Saliva Attack
summary: Lets the Lunar channel Essence into his digestive system, transforming his stomach acids into a lethal ranged weapon.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar channels Essence into his digestive system, momentarily transforming his stomach acids into a lethal weapon. He can spit this corrosive phlegm at a target within 10 yards. The attack uses Dexterity + Thrown or Athletics with a -1 accuracy modifier. The opponent may dodge but cannot parry. The attack inflicts 8L + extra successes. The Burning Saliva Attack continues to harm the opponent each turn until it is washed off or otherwise removed. Scraping the acid off requires a Dexterity + Athletics roll and is not a reflexive action — the victim or one of his associates must use a dice action to do so, though she need not roll. Rather than directly attacking an enemy with his acid saliva, the Lunar can target the opponent's weapon. The accuracy of such attacks is -2, and rather than the opponent soaking the damage, her weapon must do so. Its soak is equal to its damage value (so a straight sword that inflicts +3L has a soak of 3). Roll unsoaked damage dice normally, and every two successes reduce the weapon's damage value by one. If the weapon's damage reaches 0, the weapon is rendered useless. The acid continues to harm the weapon.

name: Cobra Eye Method
summary: Lets a Lunar adjust the lethality of his acid saliva, trading damage for the ability to precisely target an opponent's Physical Attributes, Appearance or Perception instead of dealing full damage.
description: A Lunar may attack as per Burning Saliva Attack (range 10 yards, accuracy -1, damage 8L + extra successes, opponent may not parry), and if the attack succeeds, his player rolls damage normally. However, instead of inflicting lethal health-level damage, such an attack reduces the target's Physical Attributes (Strength, Dexterity and Stamina), his Appearance or his Perception by one for every rolled health level of damage the Lunar chooses to sacrifice for this effect. An Attribute cannot be reduced below 1. An Exalt requires a week of healing to recover each Attribute point lost, but such injuries are permanent if inflicted on mortals.

name: Deadly Viper Strike
summary: Lets the Lunar create and use a more toxic variant of the venom used in the Adder Fang Method, adding lingering poison to an unarmed attack.
description: Usable as part of an unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. In addition to the normal attack damage, the venom injected causes injury and pain; the immediate damage is less than Adder Fang Method's, but if the attack succeeds, the victim's player must roll Stamina + Endurance against a difficulty equal to the Lunar's Essence. If the roll fails, the target suffers an automatic level of lethal damage and his player must roll again (at the same difficulty) next turn. Success means no injury, and any additional successes reduce the difficulty of resisting the poison next turn. If the difficulty reaches 0, the poison is no longer effective. A botch indicates the target suffers two automatic levels of lethal damage, and the difficulty of resisting next turn increases by one.

name: Rabid Beast Bite
summary: Turns a Brawl or Martial Arts bite attack into a vector for infection, risking disease in any wound it causes.
description: Functions as per Deadly Viper Strike, attacking at -1 accuracy at a range of 10 yards, but instead of inflicting lethal damage the target is rendered insensate: he may suffer sufficient bashing damage to be incapacitated, or the toxin may shock him into unconsciousness. The latter may happen if the number of bashing health levels inflicted by a single attack exceeds the target's Stamina Attribute. If it does, the target's player must make a reflexive Stamina + Endurance roll against a difficulty equal to the Lunar's Essence. If the target fails the roll for their character to avoid infection on any injury caused by such an attack, wounds that would normally have a chance of infection (those inflicting lethal or aggravated damage) increase the difficulty of the roll to avoid infection by the Lunar's Essence, and rolls for the unExalted to recover from the infection are also increased by the Lunar's Essence. The difficulty of avoiding infection from bashing damage is 1. The cost of this Charm must be paid before the Lunar makes his attack roll. Using the Rabid Beast Bite on another Lunar is considered a sign of great disrespect.
reviewFlags: Summary paraphrases the book's own somewhat run-on description of the infection mechanic; the core effect (rendering the target insensate/infectious via bite) is clear, but the exact resolution order of the two Stamina + Endurance rolls described on the page reads ambiguously and may warrant a closer re-read before promotion.

name: Form-Destroying Touch
summary: A punishing unarmed attack that implants a fragment of the Lunar's protean power in the target, causing wild, spreading mutation and eventual dissolution if left untreated.
description: Activated when the Lunar makes an unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack. The Charm has no effect at first if the attack roll fails or if the target blocks or dodges the attack — the target takes no effect, and the motes and Willpower are lost. However, if the attack lands, the player's rolled damage successes equal to or exceeding the target's Stamina are recorded as no actual health-level damage but instead implant the Lunar's protean power in the victim; the phantom damage does not end with the scene like normal damage. The target of a successful attack suffers no ill effects for the first day after she has been infected, though normal Essence is already at work. Each day after the first, anomalies begin to emerge, and the target must attempt to resist the corruption (roll Stamina + Endurance against a difficulty equal to the Lunar's Essence). If the roll succeeds, she resists its effects for that day. If the roll fails, she suffers aggravated damage; the first time this happens the damage is a single die, but it increases to two dice the second time the roll fails, three the third, and so on, as the contagion continues to spread its mutations and damage. These damage dice are rolled normally. If the number of contagion-inflicted aggravated health levels exceeds the victim's Essence + Stamina, the victim's body loses cohesion, and she dies, transmuted into a chaotic jumble of mutated organs and protoplasmic sludge. Form-Destroying Touch cannot be used on those immune to shapeshifting (such as Lunars) or where a Charm or sorcery prevents the Lunar from touching the target or shields the target from Wyld mutation. Mortal medicine is powerless to cure the Form-Destroying Touch, though Charms such as Bodily Regeneration Prana can negate the effect of the Charm if they cure all the aggravated damage from the character's health track. Disease-curing Charms and magical remedies do nothing unless they are of incredible power (the legendary Panacea Pipe might cure an afflicted character, for example). The notable exception is the cure-all Sweet Cordial (see Exalted, p. 336), which allows the victim's player a regular Stamina + Resistance roll at difficulty 1 to defeat the infection.

name: Snake Head Defense
summary: Lets a Lunar reshape part of his body — usually his hair or a tail — into one or many venomous snakes that fight semi-independently to defend him.
description: The snake-buds can be as long as half the Lunar's Essence in yards (rounded down), and there can be one large snake or many smaller ones. Though limited in reach to half the Lunar's Essence (rounded down), the snakes can attack targets of the Lunar's choosing and act on the Lunar's initiative. The snake-extensions fight with half (round down, minimum 1) the Lunar's Attribute and Ability scores and do Strength + 1L base damage. They act every turn but can split their die pool normally. Rather than the raw strength of the Exalt, a serpent's bite is venomous, acting in the same manner as the Deadly Viper Strike (see above). The venom is less than the Lunar's own, and the victim's player need only resist Stamina + Endurance against a difficulty equal to half the Lunar's Essence (rounded down, minimum 1). A snake may be attacked independently of the Lunar and has 3 health levels: -1, -2 and -4. A fourth point of damage 'kills' or disables these snakes. These wounds do not affect the Lunar while the snake remains in existence, but if he chooses to discontinue the Charm while any wounds suffered by the character's ophidian offshoots transfer to the Lunar, half (round up) of any wounds suffered by the character's ophidian offshoots transfer to the Lunar. Damaged snakes heal at the same rate as an Exalt (not as fast as the Lunar using the Charm); dead snakes do not heal. While a snake remains 'alive,' a Lunar Exalted cannot be subjected to an unanticipated attack by a visible foe. The snakes cannot parry or dodge, but a Lunar whose snake-extensions are attacked can parry or dodge the attack as if it were against the Lunar himself. A Lunar cannot use this Charm more than once at a time on himself.
reviewFlags: This row sits between Form-Destroying Touch and Monkey Arm Style in the book but is absent from the earlier OCR-only draft index used to plan this pass; visually confirmed present on printed p. 141/PDF 144.

name: Monkey Arm Style
summary: Lets a Lunar extend his reach by elongating one or both arms into long, sinuous, snake-like limbs that remain fully functional.
description: Ordinarily, a Lunar can only attack targets within arm's reach. Monkey Arm Style allows the Lunar to surprise his opponents by extending his reach by a number of yards equal to his Essence. The Charm causes one or both of the Lunar's arms to elongate, reshaping bone and muscle to create a long, sinuous limb that, despite its snake-like appearance, remains fully functional. The hand can grasp objects or targets but lacks the finesse required to wield a weapon effectively. The Monkey Arm Style can be used on its own to extend the Lunar's reach for an instant, but it is most commonly used as part of a Brawl or Martial Arts attack, allowing the character to make unarmed attacks or wrestling maneuvers at a distance equal to his Essence in yards.

name: Startling Tentacle Attack
summary: Splits one of the Lunar's limbs into multiple writhing tentacles, each able to make a separate unarmed attack at full dice pool against targets within reach.
description: Allows the Lunar to pour Essence into one of his limbs, which splits into multiple, writhing tentacles. Anything held in that limb is dropped, and while the Exalted's natural weaponry functions as normal, the damage is always converted to bashing before it is applied to the target. Each of the tentacles is capable of making a separate attack at the Lunar's full Dexterity + Brawl or Martial Arts dice, although all must attack the same target within a number of yards equal to twice the Lunar's Essence. If the defender dodges, make one roll and apply it to all attacks. However, parry attempts must be made against each attack. The tentacles re-form into the original limb after the attacks are made. The Exalted cannot create more tentacles than his permanent Essence.

name: Grasping Pseudopod Method
summary: Reshapes one of the Lunar's limbs into a single, powerful tentacle that grants an edge at clinching, holding and throwing opponents.
description: The Lunar shapes one of his limbs into a single, powerful tentacle that allows him to make clinch, hold and throw attacks out to yards equal to twice the Lunar's Essence (per the clinch/grapple rules elsewhere in Exalted). If the Lunar's player botches an attack roll if the target gets five or more successes in a contest related to the wrestling, the Lunar's player must have his character thrown toward the target and suffer the effects of being knocked down.
reviewFlags: The botch-consequence sentence in the source text reads awkwardly (possibly print/OCR damage around 'botches an attack roll if the target gets five or more successes'); paraphrased faithfully but flagged for a closer re-read before promotion.

name: Tentacle-Spear Strike
summary: Lets the Lunar strike targets at incredible range by committing more Essence to lengthen his tentacles, splitting attacks across multiple foes.
description: By increasing the amount of Essence he commits when creating tentacles, the Lunar can strike at targets further away, allowing him to make hand-to-hand attacks at incredible range. The Lunar can make a number of tentacle attacks up to his permanent Essence, and each tentacle may make a separate attack at the Lunar's full Dexterity + Brawl or Martial Arts, adding 1 die for each tentacle formed. Each tentacle may attack the same target, or they may attack different victims, but each defender must be within a number of yards of the Lunar (the Lunar's Essence x 10). Roll each attack separately, but if the target parries or dodges an attack, make one roll and apply it to all attacks directed against him. As a result, the Lunar's opponent may avoid some, all, or none of the tentacles. The tentacles re-form in the original limb immediately after the attacks are made.

name: Weapon-Snatching Coils
summary: Uses tentacles to entangle and disarm an opponent's weapon rather than to attack the opponent directly.
description: By directing his pseudopodia at an opponent's weapon, the Lunar can use the multiplicity of the tentacles and their speed and reach to foil the opponent's attacks. The maximum number and reach of the tentacles is as per the Tentacle-Spear Strike (Essence x 10 in yards, no more than Essence tentacles), but rather than rolling Dexterity + Brawl, the Lunar's player rolls Strength + Brawl, adding 1 die for each tentacle formed. The opponent may seek to parry or dodge the attack, but if the number of successes remaining after defense still exceeds the target's Dexterity, she is disarmed.

name: Bear Embrace Method
summary: Reinforces the Lunar's grappling by letting him add bought dice to a single wrestling attack, or use extra points to extend or escalate a clinch.
description: Lunars revel in the visceral nature of hand-to-hand combat, particularly when they feel the breath of their opponents on their face. As a consequence, grappling is a favored technique. This Charm allows the Lunar's player to fortify his musculature, purchasing additional dice up to the character's Dexterity when rolling a single wrestling attack with Martial Arts or Brawl. The Charm allows the addition of dice to enact, continue or escape from such maneuvers or to do extra points of damage in a clinch attack.

name: Mighty Bear Crush
summary: Imbues the Lunar's muscles with the strength and consistency of steel, converting a successful clinch, tackle or throw into automatic bonus damage successes.
description: This Charm allows the Lunar to imbue his muscles with Essence, giving flesh and bone the strength and consistency of steel hawsers. When the character has successfully executed a clinch, tackle or throw or is doing damage from maintaining a clinch, this Charm allows the Lunar to transform dice up to his Strength into automatic damage successes. The maximum number of dice the Lunar can transform is equal to the Essence or Strength, whichever is lower. The Essence for this Charm is spent after soak is applied, so characters need not worry about wagering Essence. The Mighty Bear Crush can be used against any target the Lunar perceives, including dematerialized spirits.

name: Spine-Breaking Technique
summary: Converts a successful clinch attack into a devastating, hard-to-escape lethal assault, adding automatic successes against escape attempts.
description: The pinnacle of their wrestling abilities, the Spine-Breaking Technique demonstrates the awesome power of the Lunar's bestial nature. By means of this Charm, the Lunar turns a painful and often incapacitating attack into a lethal demonstration of his prowess. The Lunar makes a clinch attack as normal, but rather than the normal bashing damage, the Spine-Breaking Technique inflicts lethal damage. The Spine-Breaking Technique is also very difficult for the victim to escape from, and a Lunar who activated the technique with his last action adds his Strength's successes to the roll to resist any escape attempt. A Lunar caught in a clinch may activate this Charm on his action to escape. The Spine-Breaking Technique can be used in a Combo with Charms that increase his Strength but not with any that enhance Dexterity.

name: Throat-Baring Hold
summary: Lets a Lunar deliberately expose himself while holding a foe, opening his own defenses in exchange for maintaining and worsening the hold turn after turn.
description: Lunars revel in close combat, and there are times when it is unwise to place themselves in a disadvantageous position while doing so will aid their hunting companions. Indeed, doing so is seen by many as both a test of strength and courage. The Throat-Baring Hold allows a Lunar who has his opponent in a hold to 'open' the opponent's defenses to other attackers. The Lunar must have a successful hold attack. Any extra successes reduce the target's lethal and bashing soak totals until the Lunar's next action or until the opponent breaks free. As with normal hold attacks, the Lunar's attack does not inflict damage. The Throat-Baring Hold may be maintained for multiple turns, but the Lunar must spend 5 motes and his action for the turn (and Charm) to maintain the Charm, and the target may break out, as if it were a normal hold. The penalty inflicted remains the same from turn to turn, until the hold is broken — a Lunar whose initial attack fares poorly must release his foe and apply the hold again for a new result. In all turns after the initial, the Lunar's player may add the Exalt's Strength as automatic successes to the roll for combating the target's escape attempts and for reducing soak totals for the purposes of the Charm. Attacks against the target will not harm the Lunar — the Charm keeps him clear of the incoming strikes — but a botched attack may still strike him.

name: Hyena Jaw Technique
summary: Available only in beastman form, this Charm lets the Lunar clamp his jaws on a held opponent's throat to quickly subdue or kill him via Stamina drain and Mental Attribute damage.
description: Activating the Hyena Jaw Technique allows a Lunar who has his opponent in a clinch or hold to subdue the foe quickly. The Charm, usable only in beastman form, allows the Lunar to extend his neck and muzzle, allowing him to clamp his jaws on the opponent's throat. Every turn the Charm is in effect, the target loses a dot of temporary Stamina and falls unconscious if reduced to 0 Stamina. If the target attempts to break away from the clinch or hold, he must soak lethal damage equal to the Lunar's Strength + 2, irrespective of the (successful or otherwise) of her player's escape roll. If the target falls unconscious as a result of Stamina loss or her injuries, further damage inflicted by the Hyena Jaw Technique reduces one of the target's Mental Attributes (Perception, Intelligence or Wits) by one, not below 0. If all four targeted Attributes are reduced to 0, the target dies. A victim of Hyena Jaw Technique regains one Attribute dot per day.

name: Cunning Porcupine Defense
summary: Sprouts razor-sharp spines from the Lunar's beastman-form body, punishing anyone who clinches, holds or grapples with him, and converting the Lunar's own unarmed attacks to lethal damage.
description: Though reveling in close combat, there are times Lunars seek to escape the clutches of their opponents and brute strength is not enough. This Charm, which can only be used when in the hybrid beastman form, allows the Lunar to give his foe a deadly surprise. Activating the Charm, the Lunar sprouts a number of 6-inch, razor-sharp spines. Anyone who clinches, holds or otherwise engages in wrestling with the Lunar, risks grave injury. Those clinching or holding the Lunar suffer damage equal to the Lunar's Strength + 5L, and the Lunar substitutes this for his normal damage when he does damage in a clinch. Any unarmed attacks made by the Lunar while the spines are extended inflict lethal damage rather than bashing. Players of characters who make unarmed attacks against a Lunar using the Cunning Porcupine Defense must make a reflexive Dexterity + Athletics roll (Difficulty 3) or else their character suffers lethal damage equal to their own Strength. Regardless, the Lunar takes damage from the opponent's attack as normal. The Cunning Porcupine Defense remains in effect as long as the Lunar commits Essence to the Charm and stays in beastman form. If the Lunar leaves beastman form or stops committing Essence, the spines merge back into his body.

name: Ossific Shard Shot
summary: Lets a Lunar tear a fragment of his own bone free, reforming his muscle around it, and hurl it at a distant target as a horrific ranged weapon.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can tear a fragment from his bones and reform his muscles to launch it from his body, hurling it at an opponent within a range of (her Perception x 10) yards. The attack is horrible to behold, as the Lunar tears free of the Lunar's body in a shower of blood and torn tissue, but it regenerates near-instantly. The attack is made with Dexterity + Archery or Thrown, at -1 accuracy, and inflicts 9L + extra successes damage.

name: Angry Rhino Charge
summary: Lets a charging Lunar overbear an opponent with sheer strength and mass, purchasing extra automatic damage-success dice up to his Strength when he lands a Brawl or Martial Arts attack after a full move.
description: Rather than simply wounding an opponent, a Lunar may use her strength and body mass to overbear the opponent and force him into a disadvantageous position. Using the Angry Rhino Charge while making a successful Brawl or Martial Arts attack allows the Lunar's player to purchase extra dice of damage up to the Exalt's Strength Attribute. These bonus dice do not add to the damage inflicted by the attack, but they do count toward determining knockdown and/or knockback (see Exalted, pp. 234-235) and also determine the difficulty of the target's roll to avoid knockdown. This Charm can only be used while the Lunar is charging into combat (that is, when the character has moved her full movement allowance for the turn) and while in beastman form.

name: Bull Head Technique
summary: Reshapes the Lunar's head into deadly, bull-like horns for the duration of a charge attack, turning a successful hit into lethal damage with purchasable bonus dice.
description: The Lunars can grow not only tentacles, but also other enhancements as well. Through the use of this Charm, the Lunar reshapes his head to be like that of a bull, including the bull's deadly horns, for the instant of an attack. While the Lunar is charging into combat (that is, has moved his full movement allowance for the turn) and makes a successful Brawl or Martial Arts attack, the player can purchase additional damage dice up to the value of the Exalt's Strength Attribute. All damage from the Bull Head Technique is lethal. Bonus damage is applied before soak, not after.

name: Subduing the Honored Foe
summary: Lets a Lunar convert a successful unarmed attack into extra automatic successes for a bashing-damage takedown rather than a killing blow, useful for capturing or ransoming a defeated foe.
description: Though Lunars enjoy the thrill of combat, they don't always want to kill their foes. In many cases, they seek simply to subdue them, as part of a ritual or gentleman-esque duel or to claim a ransom from the defeated foe. This Charm envelops the Lunar's limbs in Essence, lending his blows considerable weight but also cushioning the target from the worst of the blow. When rolling damage for an unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack, the Lunar's player can transform a number of dice up to a maximum of his character's Essence into automatic successes at the cost of 1 mote per die. Attacks enhanced with Subduing the Honored Foe automatically do bashing damage. This Charm's effects take place immediately after soak is applied, but the player must pick before he makes the attack roll how many motes he wants to spend converting dice of damage to automatic successes. If the target remains conscious after the attack but suffered more levels of bashing damage than her Stamina, she is dazed, and her player must make a successful Willpower roll (difficulty the Lunar's Strength) or have her character suffer the attack's effects.

name: Body Breaking Kata
summary: Reflects a raw, aggressive melding of strength and initiative that swells the Lunar's form to giant proportions for a single close-combat attack, doubling extra successes toward soak-piercing lethal damage.
description: Some Lunars employ finesse in combat, but most prefer brute force, and the Body Breaking Kata reflects this fact. It is not a subtle attack, but instead, employs a combination of size, strength and outright aggression to overwhelm an opponent. The Charm is only effective if the Lunar charges into close combat with her opponent — she must have moved her full movement allowance for the turn engaging the foe. The Lunar channels Essence through her body while making a single unarmed Martial Arts or Brawl attack. This Essence charge causes her form to swell and take giant proportions for an instant. As far as observers are concerned, the Exalt is charged by a monstrous version of his totem. The player of the attacking Lunar should roll Dexterity + Brawl or Martial Arts as normal for the attack but double the number of extra successes when applying the attack's soak. All damage from the Body Breaking Kata is lethal.
prerequisiteText: Bull Head Technique, Subduing the Honored Foe

name: Foot-Confusing Buffet
summary: Lets a Lunar sacrifice damage dice from a successful unarmed hit to instead penalize the target's next initiative, distracting the opponent with a dazzling flurry of light rather than injuring him.
description: Maintaining the initiative in combat is often as important as the amount of injuries inflicted on the opponent. Keeping control of the direction of a fight in the short term often takes precedence over inflicting injuries on the following turn. The Foot-Confusing Buffet allows the Lunar to keep an opponent off balance, sacrificing one or more damage dice from a successful Brawl or Martial Arts attack in favor of an initiative penalty for the foe in the following turn. The Charm surrounds the Lunar's attacking limbs with a nimbus of light, creating a mesmerizing series of patterns that distract the foe. The Lunar must activate the Charm before making his attack, paying the basic Essence cost even if the attack misses. Only if the attacking Lunar gets at least one extra success does the Foot-Confusing Buffet come into play. The Lunar may sacrifice a number of dice of damage to his Essence or Strength score, whichever is lowest. Damage dice are sacrificed before soak is applied. The number of points sacrificed is applied as a penalty to the target's player's initiative roll in the next turn.

name: Door-Breaking Method
summary: A utility Charm that lets a Lunar focus his wrath on an inanimate object, dealing devastating damage particularly effective against man-made items.
description: By means of this Charm, a Lunar can focus his wrath on an inanimate object, dealing a devastating blow to rend it into splinters. This attack is particularly effective against man-made objects, but it may be used against any non-living, non-magical item. When striking the object, the Lunar focuses his strength and aggression into the blow, as well as Essence. Every mote spent adds one die of damage to a single attack by the Lunar against an item. If the item is man-made, then each mote spent is worth two automatic damage successes instead. The Lunar's player cannot spend more motes when using this Charm than the character's Strength.

name: Hunter's Eye Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar guide an unarmed attack to a foe's weak point, permanently reducing the target's armor soak with each hit rather than damaging the target directly.
description: Strength is only part of winning a fight. Knowing where to place the opponent to gain maximum effect is an equally important consideration — perhaps more important in the case of fast, agile Lunars. Using this Charm, the Lunar guides a single unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts blow to the enemy's weak point, circumventing his armor and defenses. For every 2 motes spent, the Lunar may reduce the soak rating of her opponent's armor by 1. This applies to armor soak only — the target's natural soak is unaffected. The attack cannot reduce the soak of an opponent's armor by more than the Lunar's Dexterity or below 0. The soak reduction applies only for the enhanced single attack. This Charm is of instant duration — if the Lunar makes multiple attacks in a turn and desires to reduce the opponent's armor soak each time, she must pay for each reduction separately.

name: Armor-Rending Claw Fist
summary: Lets a Lunar permanently shred an opponent's armor rather than the opponent himself, transforming his claws into rending devices that grind down soak ratings hit after hit.
description: A Lunar's claws are formidable weapons, but the protective effects of armor can blunt the strikes of even the mightiest Exalts. By means of this Charm, a Lunar can reduce the efficacy of his opponent's armor, directing his attacks at the protective layers rather than directly at the opponent. To do so, he transforms his claws into vicious, hooked rending devices, lacking the length to cause serious harm to the opponent but granting them sufficient strength and resilience to rend the hardest armors. The Lunar makes an unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts attack as normal, including determining the amount of raw damage before soak. The opponent may reduce the attack's damage only using his armor's lethal soak rating, not his Stamina or any enhancements, unless they specifically reinforce the armor. Unlike a normal soak, this may reduce the damage of the attack to 0. Roll any remaining damage dice normally, and subtract the number of successes from all of the armor's soak ratings. This reduction is permanent, reflecting the Lunar's efforts to shred and rend the armor, though a skilled armorer may be able to affect repairs.

name: Sensing the Deadly Flow
summary: Root of the Melee Combat Charm trees; the Lunar spends Essence to guide his weapon strikes, gaining bonus attack dice on a single Melee attack.
description: By means of this Charm, a Lunar perceives the flows of Essence around his target, using them to guide his blows to best effect. For each mote of Essence spent on this Charm, the Lunar can gain an additional attack die on a single Melee attack. These bonus dice may not exceed the character's Dexterity.

name: Striking Mospid Method
summary: Root Charm feeding most of the Melee Combat I tree; the Lunar imbues his weapon with preternatural speed to buy extra initiative for a coming Melee attack.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can imbue his weapon with preternatural speed, using his Essence and instincts to enhance the tempo of his attack. When rolling initiative for a turn in which the character plans to make a Melee attack, the Lunar may spend Essence to improve his initiative for a single turn, each mote buying a +1 modifier. The character cannot spend more motes than he has points of Dexterity. The Essence cost of this Charm is paid before making the initiative roll.

name: Ferocious Biting Sword
summary: Fortifies an attacking hand-to-hand weapon with Essence, making it very difficult for a single opponent to block the attack: two successes are required to negate each of the Lunar's own successes.
description: By fortifying his attacking weapon with Essence, a Lunar can make it very difficult for his opponent to block a single attack with a hand-to-hand weapon. Players rolling to defend against this attack must roll two successes for each of the Exalt's own successes they seek to negate. If a defender rolls an odd number of successes, the extra success is wasted.

name: Dance of the Living Blade
summary: Grants the Lunar an extra action, letting him make multiple Melee attacks per turn against the same foe or against multiple foes within range, each additional attack costing Essence and using the full dice pool.
description: By using the Dance of the Living Blade, the Lunar can make multiple Melee attacks per turn. These may be against the same foe or against multiple foes within a distance in yards equal to the Lunar's Dexterity. Each additional attack costs 3 motes of Essence, and the Lunar may purchase no more additional attacks than he has points of Essence. Each attack is made with the character's full dice pool. A Lunar can buy no more extra actions than (the initiative on which he activated this Charm + 3, rounded down), but normally this means (the character's initiative + 3, rounded down). Lunars who hold their action and then invoke this Charm may lose extra actions.

name: Irresistable Storm Attack
summary: Capstone of the Dance of the Living Blade line; lets the Lunar make a number of Melee attacks equal to his Essence against multiple nearby foes at once, forcing them onto the defensive and optionally trading bonus Dexterity dice for ground.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can face multiple foes and force them onto the defensive. The Irresistible Storm Attack allows the Lunar to make a number of Melee attacks equal to his Essence. All the foes targeted by this Charm must be within a number of yards of the Lunar equal to twice his Dexterity. Each target of the Irresistible Storm Attack is subject to a full attack. In addition, for each additional mote the character spends, he may force all his opponents to either give up one yard of ground or give him a bonus Dexterity die, as per the Ferocious Avalanche Technique. The maximum number of bonus dice the character can gain is equal to his Dexterity. Each attack must be at a different foe, and no foe can be attacked more than once. Unused extra attacks are wasted. The Irresistible Storm Attack cannot be used in a Combo with Charms that grant extra attack dice or extra actions.

name: Twisting Surprise Attack
summary: Contorts the Lunar's body to automatically win initiative against a single opponent, letting the player choose when to activate it based on how the turn unfolds.
description: By suddenly transforming his body — extending his reach, adding an extra joint in an arm and so forth — the Lunar performs an "impossible" maneuver. As a result, he automatically wins initiative against a single opponent. This Charm can be activated at any point prior to the Lunar's actual action, so the player could roll initiative as normal but activate this Charm depending on the actions of others. When used in a Combo with extra action type Charms, the Twisting Surprise Attack does not need to be applied to every event in that Combo. The Twisting Surprise Attack cannot be used in a Combo with any other Charm that gives an initiative bonus.

name: Foe-Driving Attack
summary: Lets the Lunar keep attacking the same target repeatedly if his rolls exceed the target's defense by a widening margin, potentially chaining many attacks against a single foe in a turn.
description: This Charm allows the Lunar to extend his body in wild and improbable ways, keeping his off balance by force of arms and wearing down her defenses until she makes a deadly error. When activating this Charm, the Lunar's player rolls dice normally, but if the player gets 3 or more successes (not extra successes) on the attack roll, the Lunar may immediately attack that same target again. If the second attack also gets 3 successes, the Lunar can attack again, and so on, up to a maximum number of attacks equal to the Lunar's Dexterity. All attacks must be at the same target. Damage for each attack is resolved normally before the next attack is launched, unless the target has powerful defenses that will surely falter. The Foe-Driving Attack may not be used in any Combo that includes Charms that provide automatic successes on the attack roll.

name: Monkey Paw Advantage
summary: A parallel root off Sensing the Deadly Flow; lets the Lunar reroll an opponent's parried successes on a single attack for extra Essence, since the Lunar's protean weapon adjusts at the last moment.
description: The Lunar may combine his mastery of weapons and his protean nature to counter the efforts of an unwary foe, adjusting his weapon's path at the last moment to negate defensive moves. If an opponent attempts to parry a Lunar's Melee attack but does not completely block it, the Lunar's player can use the Monkey Paw Advantage to reroll the parried successes on another attack with the same weapon, paying 1 mote per die rerolled. If the opponent has actions remaining, she can attempt to parry these rerolled dice as well. The Monkey Paw Advantage confers no benefit if the target dodges. The Monkey Paw Advantage cannot be included in a Combo with Charms that give extra actions.

name: Weapon-Clutching Method
summary: Lets the Lunar elongate an arm to retrieve a dropped weapon or arm himself instantly, and reduces the difficulty of resisting disarming attempts against him.
description: Using this Charm, the Lunar can elongate one of his arms to retrieve a weapon that has been knocked from his grasp or to otherwise arm himself. The arm may extend to a number of yards equal to twice the Lunar's Essence, grabs the weapon, then returns to its normal length with the weapon ready to use. The extension and contraction of the arm are almost simultaneous, and so, the Weapon Clutching Method cannot be used to attack at a distance. Lunars who wish to make a ranged Melee attack will need to use the Surprising Gibbon Attack. In addition to proving a major advantage in weaving past an opponent's defenses, a Lunar's protean flexibility helps to make disarming opponents easy. When using this Charm, the difficulty of disarming in melee combat decreases to 2. The target may parry the attempt as usual, but his player's reflexive Wits + Melee roll requires one more success than the Lunar's disarming roll to be effective.

name: Twisting Monkey Wrist
summary: Lets the Lunar spend Essence to add dice to his own Dexterity when attempting a disarming attack, on top of Weapon-Clutching Method's lowered difficulty.
description: In addition to proving a major advantage in weaving past an opponent's defenses, a Lunar's protean flexibility helps to make disarming opponents easy. This Charm helps to make disarming attacks easy. The Lunar merely extends his limbs and alters the way her joints move in order to give her a considerable edge. When attempting a disarming attack (see Exalted, pp. 238-239), the Lunar may purchase additional dice to her Dexterity in a single attempt.

name: Surprising Gibbon Attack
summary: Lets the Lunar elongate his limbs or weapon to make a Melee attack at range, up to his Essence in yards, rather than requiring the target to be adjacent.
description: Even allowing for the reach of limbs and weapons, melee combat requires the combatants to be within a few yards of each other. Longer weapons — such as pole arms — can confer considerable advantages, particularly when facing mounted opponents. Lunar Exalted may adjust their bodies to adjust circumstances in their favor — they can elongate one or both limbs, allowing them to attack opponents some distance away. A Lunar using this Charm may attack at a distance of up to his Essence in yards. If the opponent is more than three yards from the Lunar, she will be unable to make a hand-to-hand counterattack and must move before engaging the Exalt in hand-to-hand combat. Any weapon wielded in this manner — even a knife — is considered a long weapon, and the Lunar does not suffer the usual penalties for attacking mounted opponents from on foot.

name: Spinning Blade Attack
summary: For a Lunar dual-wielding hand-to-hand weapons, lets him attack twice in a single action using his initiative for both, and abort one or both attacks into parries.
description: By means of this Charm, activated immediately after rolling initiative, a Lunar armed with two hand-to-hand weapons can attack a single opponent twice in a single turn. One action is made with each weapon. Each attack uses the Lunar's full dice pool of the character's full initiative score, and neither is considered to be with the character's off hand. The Lunar using the Spinning Blade Attack may abort one or both attacks to parries and, thus, can attack twice and, or parry twice at his full dice pool in the same turn, provided the attacks are made against the same opponent.

name: Lightning Sword Method
summary: Extends the Spinning Blade Attack so the Lunar's two dual-wielded strikes need not be directed at the same target, provided both are within normal range.
description: The Lightning Sword Method allows a Lunar armed with two weapons to attack one or two opponents in the same turn. The mechanics are as per the Spinning Blade Attack, save that both actions need not be directed against the same target, though the Lunar's attack has no greater range than normal, so both foes must be within the distance the Lunar can move for the turn.

name: Dust Devil Advance
summary: Turns the Lunar into a whirling, constantly-moving killing machine that gains bonus initiative from movement, can turn to meet an attack, and cannot be ambushed or attacked from the rear while active.
description: Using this Charm, the Lunar becomes a whirling killing machine, constantly moving and attacking, ever aware of his surroundings. While using this Charm, the Lunar gets an initiative bonus equal to half (round down) the number of yards he moved the previous turn. The Charm remains active so long as the Lunar keeps moving and commits Essence to it. If he is forced to stop moving, the Charm ends. Additionally, while the Charm is active, the Lunar can turn to meet an attack and cannot be ambushed or attacked from the rear. The Dust Devil Advance cannot be used in a Combo with any other Charm that gives an initiative bonus. This Charm cannot give the Lunar more bonus dice than his Dexterity.

name: Tiger Claw Swat
summary: A second root off Sensing the Deadly Flow; the Lunar lunges to inflict extra damage on his Melee attack, at the cost of making the attack much harder to parry or dodge with reduced effect.
description: By lunging at his foe and binding Essence into his attacks, a Lunar can inflict monstrous damage on his opponent. The Lunar may enhance a single Melee attack by buying additional damage dice at a cost of 3 motes per die. The maximum number of points that can be added to the attack is equal to the Lunar's Strength rating. This must be done before the attack is rolled. The attack can be dodged as normal, but the difficulty of parrying an attack augmented with this Charm is greatly increased. All parry attempts must first overcome a base difficulty equal to the number of dice spent fueling Tiger Claw Swat before they subtract successes from the attack. This doesn't enhance the Lunar's attack. They simply increase the difficulty of the target's parry and do not add to the damage of the Lunar's blow. The difficulty modifier is applied first and must be overcome before the extra successes can be applied to defending against the Lunar's blow. Tiger Claw Swat cannot be used in Combo with other Charms that increase damage dice.

name: Knowing Weapon Technique
summary: A second root off Sensing the Deadly Flow; makes the Lunar's weapon strikes automatically successful when the player pays Essence for remaining damage points, up to his permanent Essence.
description: By means of this Charm, a Lunar's control over his weapon is without peer, and he can steer his attack to its most deadly effect: Blades carve through flesh, and blunt weapons break bones like porcelain. After an opponent has applied his soak to an attack the Lunar makes using a hand-to-hand weapon, the Lunar may pay 3 motes of Essence per remaining damage point of damage. Each point paid for in this manner becomes an automatic success. The Lunar cannot buy more automatic successes than his permanent Essence.

name: Weapon Fusion Method
summary: A third root off Sensing the Deadly Flow; the Lunar's weapon becomes an extension of his body, letting him use his Melee, Brawl, or Martial Arts Ability (whichever is highest) to attack or parry with a hand-to-hand weapon.
description: By means of this Charm, the Lunar's weapon becomes an extension of his body. When making a single attack or parry with a hand-to-hand weapon, the Lunar's player can use his choice of the character's Melee, Brawl or Martial Arts Abilities. The weapon's characteristics are unaffected, only the Ability used to make the attack changes. The Weapon Fusion Method cannot be used as part of Combos that aid unarmed Brawl or Martial Arts combat.

name: Thunderclap Method
summary: Lets the Lunar soften a Melee attack to deal only bashing damage, or spend Essence to convert damage into automatic bashing successes, useful for subduing rather than killing.
description: Most competent swordsmen can adjust their blows so as to cause bashing damage to their targets. The Lunar Exalted are considerably more formidable than any mortal swordsman, and their Essence-laden blows can fell even a Terrestrial. By means of the Thunderclap Method, a Lunar increases the strength of a Melee attack while softening its impact, so that it will only fell an enemy, rather than slay her. A blow enhanced by this Charm rings with thunder, stunning the opponent. Any attack enhanced with this Charm automatically does only bashing damage, but after subtracting soak from the damage of the attack, the Lunar can activate this Charm and pay 1 mote of damage to change a remaining point of damage to an automatic success. Each remaining point paid for in this fashion becomes a level of bashing damage. A Lunar cannot buy more automatic successes in this fashion than he has points of Strength. The Charm cannot be part of a Combo with any other Charm that grants automatic successes.

name: Scar-Making Blow
summary: Turns the Lunar's Melee dice pool into automatic successes for a ritual, non-lethal marking attack used in Lunar society to record scars of martial standing.
description: Scars are an integral part of Lunar Exalted society, maintaining the Lunars' form and used as a means of counting coup. Scarring an opponent, without causing serious injury, is an unsubtle means of demonstrating martial superiority. A Lunar enacting this Charm can turn the Dexterity dice in his Dexterity + Melee attack pool into automatic successes when attempting to mark a target (see Exalted, p. 238).
