The opponent may parry or dodge as normal, reducing the net successes for the marking attempt. Ritual scarring forms part of several Lunar events, and the Scar-Making Blow is used in some cases to impart the markings. In such cases, the target willingly undergoes the marking, and the number of successes needed to mark the target is reduced to 1. Scars imparted by this Charm are simply the product of healing and lack the magical strength of those imparted by the Moon Caste's Form-Fixing Method.

name: Ferocious Avalanche Technique
summary: For each mote spent, forces the target of a Melee attack to either give ground or grant the Lunar a bonus attack die, up to his Dexterity, unless the target has not yet acted or already backed away as far as possible.
description: By making a series of swift and decisive blows, a Lunar can unbalance his opponent. By using the Ferocious Avalanche Technique, the Lunar forces his opponent to give ground. For each mote of Essence spent by the Lunar, his target must either yield a yard or allow the Lunar to gain a bonus attack die. If the opponent has not yet acted this turn or moved less than half his move allowance, he may back off as a reflexive action. If the opponent does not (or cannot) back away, the Lunar gains a bonus attack die equal to the distance the target didn't move. The maximum bonus the Lunar can gain from this attack is equal to his Dexterity, and these are Dexterity bonus dice.

name: Limb-Maiming Flourish
summary: Lets the Lunar guide the damage dice of a hit to their most crippling effect, converting 10s into two successes and optionally converting damage into a permanent Attribute-lowering injury.
description: Using the Limb-Maiming Flourish, a Lunar uses Essence to maximize the lethal effect of her weapon, guiding it to the points that will do most damage. When rolling damage, any 10s on the damage dice count as two successes. After determining the actual amount of damage inflicted, the Lunar may reduce one point of the damage dealt to reduce one instead of inflicting two health levels of damage. This may not reduce an Attribute below 1, nor may it be used to convert all damage into Attribute loss — the target must lose at least one health level per Attribute point lost. An Exalted requires a week of healing to recover each Attribute point lost, but such injuries are permanent if inflicted on mortals. Limb-Maiming Flourish cannot be used in a Combo with other Charms that increase damage dice.

name: Weapon-Shaping Prana
summary: Lets the Lunar reshape ordinary wood or bone into a serviceable hand-to-hand weapon of any pattern he can imagine, formed and maintained by committed Essence.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can pick up any piece of wood or bone and imbue it with his Essence to transform it into a serviceable hand-to-hand weapon (selected from the list on p. 327 of Exalted). It costs 2 motes to form a one-handed hand-to-hand weapon, and 3 motes to form a two-handed hand-to-hand weapon. These weapons can be used by others as well as by the Lunar and persist until the Exalt withdraws the Essence committed to the Charm.

name: Stunning Moonsilver Blow
summary: Lets the Lunar cause a moonsilver weapon attack to inflict bashing damage rather than lethal, without subtracting soak from the damage dealt, bypassing the normal pulling-blows rules.
description: The Lunar's mastery of moonsilver weapons allows her to imbue a weapon with Essence, causing it to flow and flatten, rather than crush or cut. With the use of this Charm, the Lunar can cause a single attack with a moonsilver weapon to inflict bashing damage rather than lethal without subtracting a success from her attack action, as per the normal pulling blows rules (see Exalted, p. 238).

name: Surprising Moonsilver Deformation
summary: Uses a moonsilver weapon's fluid nature to make it harder to parry or dodge a single attack, raising the successes needed against it at a cost of Essence per success.
description: Moonsilver weapons have an innate link to the Lunar Exalted, affording them considerable advantages in combat. Combining this Charm with a moonsilver weapon's fluid nature increases the difficulty of parrying or dodging it; the weapon simply flows around the opponent's defenses or anticipates the defensive moves. Increase the number of successes needed to parry or dodge a single attack with a moonsilver weapon by up to the Exalt's Essence, at a cost of 2 additional success required. This simply increase the difficulty of the target's parry roll and do not add to the damage of the target's attack. The difficulty modifier is applied first and must be overcome before the extra successes can be applied to defend against the Lunar's blow. This Charm has no effect if the parrying weapon is also made of moonsilver, nor is it effective when attacking with moonsilver talons or teeth.

name: Deadly Moonsilver Affinity
summary: Lets the Lunar buy extra damage dice for a moonsilver weapon attack up to the weapon's damage rating, with bonus dice beyond his Strength costing more Essence.
description: By means of this Charm, a Lunar can further exploit his weapon's fluid form, rendering it into a truly devastating tool, for the edge flows into blows, seeking to widen and deepen cuts or reshaping itself to smash bones for maximum effect. When making a damage roll for a moonsilver weapon, the Lunar's player can purchase additional damage dice up to the weapon's damage rating. These points are added before soak is applied. Bonus dice of damage up to the Lunar's Strength cost 1 mote each, while those that exceed the character's Strength cost 3 motes each. Deadly Moonsilver Affinity cannot be used as part of a Combo with other Charms that increase the damage dice or extra successes of an attack.

name: Insidious Moonsilver Shard
summary: Capstone of the Moonsilver line; empowers a moonsilver weapon so a successful hit lodges a lethal shard fragment in the victim that causes ongoing damage each day until surgically removed.
description: A moonsilver weapon's edge is its most lethal aspect, inflicting heinous damage on the Lunar's foes. It is not, however, the only harm such weapons can inflict. A more insidious option is open to appropriately minded Lunars. By activating this Charm, the Lunar empowers his moonsilver weapon so that it gains a purpose even beyond what lies in his hands. If the blow is successful, a fragment of the blade breaks off in the wound, remaining to cause grievous harm to the victim. The player must pay for the Charm before the attack action. For the magic to have effect, the attack must be successful and must inflict at least one health level of damage. The attack does damage as normal, but the sliver of moonsilver remains in the wound, slowly working its way through the victim's body. This causes one die of lethal damage per day and continues to cause damage until it is removed. Removing the shard requires at least Medicine 3 and a Challenging (requires 3 successes) procedure to remove five dice of lethal damage, minus one die per extra success (to a minimum of 1L). Charms that heal aggravated damage, such as Bodily Regeneration Prana, can also be used to expel a moonsilver shard, as can a shapeshifting stunt. Activating this Charm lowers the weapon's damage rating by 1 until the next time the wielder rests.
prerequisiteText: Surprising Moonsilver Deformation, Deadly Moonsilver Affinity

name: Eagle Eye Advantage
summary: Root of the Ranged Combat Charm trees; sharpens the Lunar's hand-eye coordination, granting extra dice on a single ranged attack.
description: A Lunar Exalted can use this Charm to sharpen his ranged hand-eye coordination, making it easier to strike ranged targets. Careful observers (a reflexive Perception + Awareness roll, difficulty 3) will notice a change in the Lunar's eyes — they take on an avian aspect — but otherwise, his form is unchanged. When making an Archery or Thrown attack against a ranged target, the Lunar may convert attack dice into automatic successes. He may not, however, purchase more successes than his Dexterity score.

name: Nature's Harmony Advantage
summary: By listening to his animal instincts, lets the Lunar ignore all environmental penalties (wind, rain, etc.) on a single Archery or Thrown attack, though it must be included in a Combo with Wolf Eye Advantage to also offset visibility penalties.
description: By listening to his animal instincts, a Lunar can compensate for adverse environmental effects such as wind and rain on the flight path of his missile. The arrow always flies true, allowing the Exalt to ignore all environmental penalties for ranged attacks. Nature's Harmony Advantage does not compensate for reduced visibility and must be included in a Combo with the Wolf Eye Advantage if the Lunar is to avoid all environmental penalties for ranged attacks.

name: Knowing the Arrow's Path
summary: Ignores cover penalties (including from shields) when firing at an opponent, since the Lunar's enhanced senses degrade the effectiveness of any cover the target uses against a missile attack.
description: Cover is a target's best defense against missile attacks, but the preternaturally enhanced senses and reflexes of the Lunar Exalted can degrade its effectiveness. Using Knowing the Arrow's Path allows the Lunar to ignore cover penalties, including those of a shield, when firing at an opponent.

name: Two-Target Method
summary: Lets the Lunar split a single missile attack roll's successes between two targets standing near each other, by shooting through the first target into the second.
description: By using his Essence to alter the arrow's flight, a Lunar can attack two targets with a single arrow, usually by shooting through the first target into the second. Both victims must be within two yards of each other. The Lunar's player makes a single Archery + Dexterity attack roll. If it succeeds, the successes are split as equally as possible between the two targets, who each may attempt to parry or dodge as normal. If the Lunar's player rolls only one success, he picks who he attacks.

name: Skillful Ricochet Attack
summary: Negates an opponent's cover for a single Thrown or Archery attack by bouncing the missile off a surface, though each bounce subtracts from the attack's damage.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can negate an opponent's cover by bouncing his missile off of several surfaces, his enhanced senses allowing him to calculate an unerring trajectory for a single Thrown or Archery attack. Each surface the missile bounces off of subtracts 1 from the attack's damage (meaning the character's Strength + the weapon's damage bonus). If the total damage reaches 0, the weapon's energy is spent, and it falls to the ground.

name: Finding the Needle's Eye
summary: Lets the Lunar make a reflexive missile-on-missile deflection attempt against an inbound ranged attack aimed at himself, reducing the attacker's successes.
description: To an Exalt who can hit a dipping swallow at 100 yards, striking a projectile in flight is only slightly more challenging. Using this Charm, the Lunar can attempt to deflect a missile aimed at him by using a missile of his own. To attempt this, the Lunar must have the bow and ammunition ready. The player makes a reflexive Dexterity + Archery or Thrown roll, with each success reducing the attacker's successes. If the Lunar's player rolls at least as many successes as the attacker, the attack is disrupted and causes no damage. If the Lunar's player does not equal or exceed the attacker's successes, then the attacker's successes are still reduced. This defense is only effective against ranged attacks, and the Lunar must expend one arrow per activation of this Charm.

name: Arrow-Breaking Shot
summary: Extends Finding the Needle's Eye to protect allies rather than just the Lunar himself, requiring the deflector's successes to exceed the attacker's rather than merely equal them.
description: While Finding the Needle's Eye allows an Exalt to use arrows to defend himself from enemy missile attacks, protecting his allies is a much more difficult task. Not only must the Lunar observe the path of projectiles inbound against multiple targets, but firing at crossing targets often requires him to hit a crossing target, not an issue when the Lunar himself was the target. The Arrow-Breaking Shot functions like Finding the Needle's Eye, save that each deflection attempt costs more Essence and requires the number of successes to exceed those of the attacker for the deflection to be successful. As with Finding the Needle's Eye, the Charm can be used only against ranged attacks, and the Lunar must expend one arrow with each activation of the Charm.

name: Silver Waterfall Technique
summary: Lets the Lunar make multiple extra Archery or Thrown attacks in a turn by shifting his body with fluid grace, each attack at a target the player declares in advance.
description: Shifting her body to give it an efficient, fluid grace, a Lunar archer can load and fire her bow with preternatural speed. For every 3 motes spent activating the Charm, the Lunar can make an additional Thrown or Archery attack, which may be at her first target or at another target in range. This normally means (the character's initiative + 3), but Lunars who hold their action and then invoke this Charm may lose extra actions. Each attack uses the character's full dice pool. The character cannot make an attack unless she has the ammunition to do so. Regardless of how the attack is described, determine the arrow's damage normally against target hit (i.e., arrows boosted by this Charm are not "slowed down" by passing through the chest of the first target, beyond dividing the successes of the attack).

name: Rain of Feathered Doom
summary: Capstone of the Two-Target Method line; lets the Lunar fire a barrage of arrows at multiple targets within an area at once, limited by his rate of fire and available ammunition.
description: Using this Charm to speed his drawing and firing, the Lunar can loft a series of arrows before the first has hit its target. Unlike regular shots, the Rain of Feathered Doom targets an area, rather than an individual. The Lunar may fire as many arrows as (his Dexterity x the rate of the bow), subject to the number of arrows and motes of Essence available. For every two arrows fired, the Lunar may target one individual, and each individual targeted costs 2 motes of Essence. All of the targets must be within (the Lunar's Dexterity) yards to of a center point picked by the Lunar. The targets do not gain the benefits of any movement or cover, so thick do the arrows fly. Make one attack roll, and apply it to all the targets, increasing the base difficulty of each target by 1. Irrespective of the number of arrows fired, the Lunar may attack each target only once during the turn (the extra arrows are wasted).

name: Arrow-Shaping Method
summary: Lets the Lunar transform raw materials into functional ammunition or thrown weapons on the fly, never running out of ammunition; combines the Body Enhancement/Shapechanging line's material sense with ranged combat.
description: So long as he is surrounded by raw materials — stones, twigs, bones, reeds, long blades of grass and the like — a Lunar will not run out of ammunition. Instead of drawing arrows from his quiver, the Lunar may instead pick up an appropriate piece of raw material — anything long and thin for arrows, and anything of roughly the correct shape for thrown weapons — and transform it into a missile suitable for firing from the bow or for throwing. The arrow retains the appearance of the raw material, but in the hands of the Lunar, it is a functional but nonmagical item of that type. Only the Lunar can use weapons he has shaped. He can shape a maximum number of missiles equal to his Dexterity in a single turn and must use them within a number of turns equal to his Essence, for at the end of that time they revert to their raw form. Missiles embedded in their victims when they revert do an extra 1L damage.
prerequisiteText: Shaping the Once-Living Form, Nature's Harmony Advantage

name: Wolf Eye Advantage
summary: Lets the Lunar treat visibility ranges as double their actual value for a single Archery or Thrown attack, offsetting poor visibility from fog, darkness, or similar conditions.
description: By sharpening his senses, a Lunar can offset the disadvantage of poor visibility (but not for the effects of wind, rain and the like) on a missile's flight path. Activating this Charm allows the Lunar to treat visibility ranges as double their value for the purposes of a single Archery or Thrown attack. For example, on a foggy day the Lunar can attack targets without penalty out to 20 yards and with +1 difficulty out to 60 yards. Furthermore, when using this Charm, a Lunar can make a blind attack out to 200 yards, and treats all night conditions as day (further including increasing visibility distances). See page 237 of Exalted for the visibility table.

name: Wind-Wings Carry Technique
summary: Lets the Lunar shoot at up to twice a weapon's listed range for reduced dice penalties, up to four times its range at a steeper penalty, without benefiting hitting small targets at shorter range.
description: Range is the main enemy of archers, but by enhancing his senses to observe the flows of Essence within the air, the Lunar can use them to steer the shot to the target. The Lunar can attack out to two times the weapon's listed range at -1 die and out to three times the weapon's range at only -2 dice. Additionally, a Lunar using this Charm can strike attack targets out at four times the weapon's range at -4 dice. This Charm confers no benefits to hitting small targets at shorter distances.

name: Bow-Bending Method
summary: Lets the Lunar strengthen a bow beyond its normal draw limit for a single shot without breaking it, risking the bow snapping on a failed roll if pushed too far past its rated maximum.
description: All bows have a pull, and beyond this upper limit, the archer's strength has no appreciable effect, except perhaps to break the bow. Using this Charm to control his actions and Essence to reinforce the weapon, the Lunar can coax extra performance out of the bow. When firing, the Lunar player must state the Strength the Lunar is using and can be as much as double a bow's maximum Strength without harming the weapon. The player may increase the maximum beyond double, but doing so requires him to make an immediate — before the shot is fired — reflexive Dexterity + Archery roll against a difficulty equal to the number of points by which he exceeded the weapon's maximum Strength. If he succeeds, the shot takes place as usual. If he fails, the bow breaks, and the Essence is wasted. If making multiple missile attacks, this Charm must be activated once for each shot, as usual for instant Charms.

name: Body-Pinning Style
summary: Uses precision targeting rather than brute force to increase archery damage; 10s on the damage roll count as two successes, without regard to the Lunar's unmodified Strength.
description: While the Bow Bending Method attempts to use brute force to increase archery damage, the Body-Pinning Style relies on precision targeting as can only be provided by someone with the body control of a Lunar Exalted. When rolling damage dice for an archery attack, count all 10s as two successes. The number of successes gained in this way cannot exceed the Lunar's unmodified Strength.

name: Lightning Stroke Attack
summary: Makes a single ranged attack impossible to dodge or parry — the target must instead soak the damage, a defense proof even against the Solar Exalted's perfect defenses.
description: Some attacks are so swift and powerful that the target doesn't see them coming and has no chance to avoid it. Ranged attacks incorporating the Lightning Stroke Attack exploit the opponent's eye by warping limbs and the missile in flight. The attack is rolled normally, but to this end, misdirecting the opponent's eye to warp limbs and the missile in flight, the target cannot attempt to dodge or parry. Instead, she must rely on her soak to absorb the arrow's damage. The perfect defenses of the Solar Exalted, Charms such as Seven Shadow Evasion and Heavenly Guardian Defense, are proof against this attack, just as they are proof against all others.

name: Riding the Secret Wind
summary: Lets the Lunar make a ranged Thrown or Archery attack at any target within his weapon's range, even without line of sight, by tapping into the flows of Essence and the senses of nearby beasts.
description: By using this Charm, the Lunar can tap into the flows of Essence and the senses of beasts in the area to target any opponent within reach of his weapon. He may attack any target in range with a single Thrown or Archery attack, even if no direct line of sight exists between Lunar and target, as long as there is some unblocked route the missile could take to the target, it will attempt to strike the victim. The normal range penalties apply, but the target cannot claim any cover modifiers. The target may parry or dodge the attack normally, but is unlikely to be aware of it and, so, probably cannot blindside. Riding the Secret Wind cannot be included in a Combo with any Charms that have automatic damage successes.

name: Deadly Assassin's Shot
summary: Capstone of the Ranged Combat II tree; gives the ranged attack a bloodthirsty life of its own, causing wounds that keep bleeding as automatic successes turned into ongoing damage until soaked.
description: By allowing his subconscious mind control and shaping his body to the needs of the shot, the Lunar can fire a truly devastating ranged attack against a single foe. The powerful Charm gives to the arrow a bloodthirsty life of its own, its erratic path leaving jagged wounds and, occasionally, amputating limbs. Immediately after soak is applied, the Lunar can spend motes of Essence into the mechanical effect of turning damage dice into automatic successes. The maximum number of automatic successes cannot exceed the Lunar's permanent Essence or the maximum Strength rating of the bow, whichever is lower.

name: Steel Paw Style
summary: Root of the Defensive I tree; briefly hardens the Lunar's hands and forearms to iron so he can parry hand-to-hand or ranged attacks unarmed, though with no bonus.
description: By means of this Charm, the Lunar focuses Essence into the skin of his hands and forearms, briefly causing them to become iron-hard. This allows the Lunar to parry hand-to-hand or ranged attacks, even if unarmed, though it confers no bonus to the parry and cannot be used as part of an offensive action.

name: Ground-Denying Defense
summary: Lets the Lunar spend Essence before initiative to reduce the maximum number of opponents who can attack him in a turn, using terrain and instinct to limit access.
description: In clear terrain, up to five opponents can attack a single target in a turn. By using the Ground-Denying Defense to focus his instincts, a Lunar can use the terrain and the opponent's own actions to limit the number of attackers he faces in a given turn. For every 2 motes spent, the Lunar can reduce the maximum number of opponents able to attack him in a turn by one. Essence spent to activate this Charm must be spent before initiative is rolled for the turn. The Lunar has no control over which opponent he avoids -- those with the highest initiative values are still able to attack, while those with lower initiative scores are evaded -- nor can he reduce the maximum number of attackers by more than his Dexterity or below one. The Ground-Denying Defense can be used in any terrain, even open ground. If the terrain naturally reduces the number of potential attackers, for example a narrow passage, the Ground-Denying Defense reduces the modified maximum number of attackers for that terrain but still cannot reduce the value below one. Example: a Lunar with Dexterity 3 could reduce the maximum number of opponents he faces by three at a cost of 6 motes; facing five enemies, the two with the highest initiative totals could still attack him, and facing only three opponents, two would still be able to attack him, since the Charm reduces the maximum number of attackers, not the actual number. In a narrow tunnel that already allows a maximum of two attackers, the Lunar would only need to spend 2 motes to reduce the number of attackers to one.

name: Golden Tiger Block
summary: Lets a dexterous Lunar convert dice in a parry attempt into automatic successes, up to his Dexterity, even dealing lethal damage on the parry while unarmed.
description: The preternatural speed of a Lunar Exalted gives him a substantial advantage when seeking to parry an opponent's attacks. Indeed, a sufficiently dexterous Lunar can use the Golden Tiger Block to render himself almost unassailable. When making a parry, he may spend 1 mote to convert a die into an automatic success. He may only purchase as many automatic successes as he has points of Dexterity in that pool. A Lunar using the Golden Tiger Block may deal lethal damage even if unarmed.

name: Wary Swallow Method
summary: Lets a Lunar parry an attack he is not consciously aware of, such as one from the rear or from an invisible attacker, using instinct in place of full dice-pool advantage.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can attempt to parry an attack directed at him, even if he is unaware of it (for example, an attack from the rear or by an invisible character). The Exalt allows instinct to guide his actions and, thus, can respond to events that have yet to register in his conscious mind. The Lunar gains no advantage in the parry action, but he may use his full dice pool if he has not yet acted during the turn. The Lunar may postpone his action, but once he has taken it, he may not use Wary Swallow Method to gain a parry.

name: Feline Guard Technique
summary: Lets the Lunar parry with his full relevant Ability pool rather than a split defense pool, at the cost of forgoing dodge and most of his movement that turn.
description: Like a cat, the Lunar is always ready to respond to attacks. By means of the Feline Guard Technique, a Lunar may parry an attack with his full relevant Ability pool total (meaning Dexterity + Ability + any weapon modifiers). The character cannot activate this Charm more times in a turn than he has points of permanent Essence. A Lunar cannot dodge during a turn in which he activates the Feline Guard Technique. A Lunar may not move more than half his movement allowance. Feline Guard Technique cannot be used in any Combos that contain extra action Charms. This Charm is not effective against attacks the character is not aware of.

name: Den Mother Method
summary: Lets a Lunar who has not yet acted abort his action to parry an attack aimed at another character within range, adding his parry successes to the ally's own defense.
description: Using his superhuman reflexes, a Lunar Exalted who has yet to act can activate this Charm and abort his action to parry an attack directed at another character. This Charm is effective as long as the Lunar is aware of the attack, it is possible to parry it, and the target is within (the Lunar's permanent Essence) yards. If the Lunar has already acted, then this Charm has no effect. The Exalt uses his entire dice pool to parry the attack, and any parry successes he gets are added to those achieved by the character he is aiding.

name: Crouching Tiger Stance
summary: Capstone of the Defensive I tree; enhances a parry with bonus Dexterity dice and, if the block is total, grants an immediate reflexive counterattack with a full dice pool.
description: A skilled Lunar can turn his opponent's attack into a deadly counter, extending and twisting his limbs in a manner that allows him to go on the offensive in hand-to-hand attacks. He parries with his full dice pool plus 2 Dexterity bonus dice in the parry attempt enhanced with the Crouching Tiger Stance, and if he completely blocks the attack, the Lunar may immediately make a reflexive Melee, Martial Arts or Brawl counterattack with his full dice pool against his opponent. If he only partially parries the blow, he cannot counterattack. The Lunar must activate this Charm before he acts for the turn -- he may postpone his action, as normal, but if the Lunar has already acted, then this Charm cannot be used in the turn. The Crouching Tiger Stance confers no advantages against a ranged attack, nor can it be used to counter counterattacks or against attacks the Lunar is not aware of.

name: Bowing Reed Technique
summary: Root of the Defensive II tree; removes the multiple-dodge dice-pool penalty for the rest of the turn once the player declares a full dodge.
description: Mobility and agility are innate characteristics of the Lunar Exalted, who can use them to considerable effect when seeking to avoid damage. By activating this Charm when the player declares a full dodge, the Lunar does not suffer any dice-pool penalties for dodging multiple attacks for the rest of the turn. She may use her full Dexterity + Dodge pool against all attacks for the remainder of the turn, providing she is able to maneuver away from attacks. A Lunar rendered immobile by terrain, magic or other effects gains no advantage from Bowing Reed Technique and must rely on parry or soak to avoid the attack.

name: Bending Before the Storm
summary: Lets a Lunar convert dice on a dodge attempt into automatic successes, up to his Dexterity per attempt, letting him guarantee successes across multiple dodges in a full-dodge turn.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can use his Essence to enhance his dodging efforts, moving as gracefully as a swan and as sure-footedly as a mountain goat once activated. Before making a dodge roll, the Lunar's player may spend Essence to transform some of his dice on a dodge attempt into automatic successes at a cost of 1 mote per die converted. The player may purchase as many automatic successes as the character's Dexterity Attribute, even if circumstances -- such as making multiple dodge attempts using full dodge -- reduce the total dodge dice pool. If modifiers reduce the number of dice in the dodge pool below the character's Dexterity, then the size of the dodge pool is the maximum number of successes that may be purchased. Successes must be purchased separately for each dodge attempt, so a Lunar seeking five automatic successes on each of three dodge attempts in the same turn would spend a total of 15 motes.

name: Wind-Dancing Method
summary: Lets a Lunar who succeeds at a dodge move up to eight yards away from the attacker as part of the dodge, denying follow-up attacks unless the foe can close the distance.
description: Simply dodging an attack may not be enough to save an Exalt from harm -- his opponent may have multiple actions and may keep attacking until the character's defenses fail. Using the Wind-Dancing Method, a Lunar can use his agility to both avoid an attack and make it much harder for an opponent to press her advantage. By using this Charm, when dodging, if he succeeds in dodging an attack, the Lunar can move up to eight yards from the attacker as a reflexive part of the dodge action, even if the Lunar has already moved this turn. In hand-to-hand combat, this means the opponent must move herself or use some reach-extending magic if she wishes to attack again; if the attacker cannot reach the Lunar for her next attack, she may make no further attacks against the Lunar this turn. A Lunar who is attacked repeatedly can activate this Charm after each attack and continue moving away from the attacker, hoping to exhaust her movement. This Charm does not allow the Lunar to take a dodge action if he could not normally do so -- Lunars wishing to defend themselves without splitting their dice pools or going full dodge will have to put this Charm in a Combo.

name: Serpent Eye Defense
summary: Lets a Lunar lock eyes with an attacker to distract him, causing his attack to go wide and letting the Lunar add Charisma dice (not subject to the normal dodge-bonus ceiling) to his dodge pool.
description: By locking his eyes with his attacker and activating this Charm, the Lunar can distract his opponent and cause the attack to go wide. The attacker must be within a number of yards equal to (5 x the target's Perception) for the Charm to be effective -- the opponent needs to be able to see the Lunar's eyes for them to distract him. If the attacker does not use her visual senses -- for example, if she is blind or blindfolded -- then the Charm is wasted. If the victim is deliberately avoiding the Lunar's gaze, this increases the difficulty of all actions involving the Lunar (including attack and defense rolls) by 2, and the avoidance must be declared before the Charm is activated. Once stung, the opponent may begin avoiding the Lunar's gaze, but the target cannot suddenly decide to begin when the Lunar activates this Charm. If the Charm takes effect, the attacker is momentarily confused as to the Lunar's position, and the Lunar may add a number of dice to his dodge pool equal to his Charisma. These are not Dexterity bonus dice -- they are Charisma dice, and thus they circumvent the normal ceiling on dodge bonus dice.

name: Unmoving Bear Defense
summary: Lets an immobile Lunar still make a dodge attempt without maneuvering, twisting and deforming his body in place, adding his Essence to the dodge pool or using it as the pool if he has none.
description: Dodges usually require the defender to maneuver and are thus impossible if the character can give no ground. Using the Unmoving Bear Defense, a Lunar Exalted can make dodge attacks without moving, instead using his protean abilities to twist and deform his body to avoid the attacks. The Lunar must be conscious and able to maneuver to use this Charm, though he does not need to actually move his feet. When dodging, he may add his Essence to his dodge pool. If the character has no dodge attempt, he may use his Essence as his dice pool in a dodge attempt. This Charm is not compatible with other Charms that add dice to the character's dodge pool but does not preclude Charms that allow dodge attempts at the character's full dice pool.

name: Foot Trapping Counter
summary: Lets a Lunar in hand-to-hand combat force a difficulty roll on an opponent trying to move away from him, potentially rooting her in place; can shut down movement-based escape Charms.
description: If, during hand-to-hand combat, an opponent seeks to move away from the Lunar, he may activate this Charm to hinder her move. The opponent's player makes a reflexive Dexterity + Athletics roll against a difficulty equal to the Lunar's Dexterity. If the opponent succeeds, she may move as intended; otherwise, she must remain in the same place. This can stop Charm-powered escapes such as the Lunar Charm Wind-Dancing Method and the Terrestrial Hopping Firecracker Escape and even high-speed flyby attacks such as the Solar Eagle-Wing Style.

name: Flowing Body Evasion
summary: Lets a Lunar attempt a reflexive dodge roll against an attack that would normally be undodgeable (area effects, magically unavoidable attacks); a single success avoids the attack entirely.
description: For a dodge to be effective, the character must be able to move away from the source of possible injury. Most attacks -- a fist, a sword, an arrow -- are concentrated on a single point and, thus, are avoidable, but not all attacks. Some attacks are so magically enhanced they are unavoidable, while others affect an area, perhaps encompassing sufficient space that a character doesn't have the speed to get clear before the blow lands. In such cases, the character would ordinarily be unable to dodge to avoid the attack. However, a Lunar who knows Flowing Body Evasion may attempt to cheat fate, using speed, agility and his shapeshifting nature to avoid the attack. The exact method will vary -- perhaps the Lunar puts on a burst of speed, dodges with godlike agility, or squeezes into a tiny hole -- but the end result is the same: a nearly impenetrable defense. When the Lunar activates this Charm, his player must make a reflexive Dexterity + Dodge roll. If the player gets at least one success, the Exalt avoids the attack totally. If the roll fails, the attack affects the Lunar normally. This is a dodge attempt, so a Lunar who fails to dodge with this Charm cannot attempt to make an 'actual' dodge roll for the turn. This Charm cannot be placed in a Combo with any Charm that would cause the Lunar's player to automatically succeed on the Dexterity + Dodge roll. A Lunar can only use this Charm before he takes his action for the turn -- he may postpone his action, as normal, but once he acts, he is unable to invoke Flowing Body Evasion.

name: Pack-Saving Method
summary: Lets a Lunar abort his action to redirect an attack aimed at a nearby ally onto himself instead, via a Dexterity + Dodge roll; cheaper if the ally is bonded via Brotherhood of Lake and River.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can use his preternatural abilities to help defend his associates. If an ally is attacked, the Lunar may abort his action and seek to wrest the friend out of harm's way. The associate must be within a number of yards equal to the Lunar's Dexterity for him to be able to use the Charm, and the Lunar must pay the Essence cost as his player declares the action. The Essence cost is usually 3 motes per attempt, but if the ally is bonded to the Lunar by the Charm Brotherhood of Lake and River, the cost is only 2 motes. The Lunar's player makes a Dexterity + Dodge roll, and if the player rolls even a single success, the original target avoids taking damage from the attack; the Lunar takes the attack instead, with the dodge roll applied as a normal defense. If the roll botches, both the Lunar and the target take the attack, and neither can make any further defense against it. Lunars may use this Charm more than once in a turn, but it must be used before they take their action for the turn -- the Lunar can postpone his action, but once he has made his dice roll, he can no longer use this Charm. The shielded character cannot decline the effects of this Charm.

name: Running Through the Herd
summary: Capstone of the Defensive II tree; lets a Lunar redirect an incoming attack from himself onto a nearby target via illusion and shapeshifting, if he beats the attacker's Perception on a Dexterity + Perception roll.
description: Using a mix of Dexterity, shapeshifting and illusion to confuse his opponent, a Lunar can employ this Charm to mislead an opponent into attacking the wrong person. To use this Charm, the Lunar must be in close proximity to his intended target (who must be less than the Lunar's Dexterity in yards away). When the character is attacked, the Lunar reflexively rolls the Exalt's Dexterity + Perception; for the Charm to take effect, the Lunar's player must get as many successes as the attacker's Perception. If the Lunar succeeds, the Lunar avoids the attack and the new target is subject to it instead. The new target may attempt to parry or dodge as normal if she has actions available. If the redirection attempt fails, the Lunar takes the damage normally -- he cannot use the redirection effort. This Charm cannot be used to avoid counterattacks, nor is it compatible with Charms that cause the Lunar to gain automatic dodge successes.

name: Hide-Toughening Essence
summary: Root of the Defensive III tree; lets a Lunar purchase bonus bashing soak (up to her Stamina) at any point in the scene, with only minor cosmetic changes to her hide.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar's skin thickens and strengthens, providing the Lunar with additional soak against bashing damage. When this Charm is invoked, or as a simple action at any time later in the scene, the Lunar's player may purchase bonus points of bashing soak for her character. A player cannot purchase more points of soak than her character has dots of Stamina. The player must purchase at least one point when the Charm is activated. The Lunar's outward appearance is largely unchanged, though closer examination will show the modifications to his hide. The character can wear armor as normal while under the effects of this Charm. The Lunar's bashing soak cannot be raised above 12 by the combined effects of this Charm and Deadly Beastman Transformation's gifts and effects on the character's Stamina. Instead, the character may ignore bashing attacks that do less raw damage than the difference between 12 and what the character's soak would be without the limit. A character may never ignore attacks doing more than 12 points of raw damage, regardless of what the character's soak should be.

name: Armor-Forming Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar purchase bonus lethal soak (up to half her Stamina) by growing moonsilver-laced bony plates over her body, compatible with armor but visibly reducing her Appearance per point bought.
description: The Armor-Forming Technique creates bony plates in the Exalt's body and limbs and hides vital organs behind multiple sheets of moonsilver-laced bone. These defenses allow the character to bolster his resistance to even lethal damage. The bone grows up and around the character's armor, sealing his weak points and reinforcing his armor's strength; thus, this Charm is compatible with the use of armor. When this Charm is invoked, or at any time thereafter during the scene, the player may spend motes of Essence to purchase extra soak against lethal damage for his character. The player must purchase at least one point when the Charm is activated. The maximum number of points of soak the player can purchase is equal to half (round down, minimum of 1) his character's Stamina Attribute. Unlike the Hide-Toughening Essence, the bony growths wrought by the Armor-Forming Technique are profound and immediately obvious to any observers. Furthermore, each point purchased with the Charm reduces the character's Appearance by 1 (to a minimum of 0, at which point the character is unable to be beheld). The Lunar's lethal soak cannot be raised above 12 by the combined effects of this Charm and Deadly Beastman Transformation's gifts and effects on the character's Stamina. Instead the character may ignore lethal attacks that do less raw damage than the difference between 12 and what the character's soak would be without the limit. A character may never ignore attacks doing more than 12 points of raw damage, regardless of what the character's soak should be.

name: Limb-Shielding Growth
summary: Lets a Lunar grow a bony shield-like growth on one arm, automatically reducing an attacker's success dice by one against hand-to-hand and ranged attacks, at the cost of a die penalty on attacks made with that hand.
description: Using this Charm, the Lunar can cause a large bony growth to appear on one of his arms (usually the hand). He can use this 'shield' to protect his body from hand-to-hand and ranged attacks alike, gaining the benefits of a targeted shield, automatically reducing an attacker's success dice by one. The Lunar does not suffer a mobility penalty for using Limb-Shielding Growth, nor does he need to add to his fatigue value, but any attacks made using the hand upon which the shield has grown are at -1 dice.

name: Scales of the Dragon
summary: Lets a Lunar grow moonsilver-reinforced dragon scales for a scene, granting a large soak bonus like articulated plate armor; incompatible with worn armor but stackable with Hide-Toughening Essence, Armor-Forming Technique, and a carried shield.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can transform his hide to resemble that of a ferocious Celestial dragon. His body is covered with overlapping moonsilver-reinforced scales that glisten coldly in the light and provide formidable protection against all forms of attack. It is as if the character is swathed in articulated plate armor, and the Lunar gains a +9L/+9B soak bonus, while incurring only a -1 mobility penalty. The armor has no fatigue value, and it is not counted as armor for the purposes of attacks that ignore armor, but it does count as armor for the purposes of stopping aggravated attacks. Unlike the other armor-enhancing Charms known to the Lunar Exalted, Scales of the Dragon is not compatible with the use of armor. However, the character's player continues to count her character's Stamina (or half Stamina against lethal damage) as she gains the benefits of a shield; the Lunar still gains the benefits of a shield if carried, and can reinforce her defense with Hide-Toughening Essence and Armor-Forming Technique. No combination of this Charm, those two Charms, and the effects of Deadly Beastman Transformation can increase either of the character's natural soaks above 12. If the character's soak would rise above 12, then the character will ignore attacks that have raw damage less than the difference between 12 and what the Lunar's soak should be, to a maximum of 12.

name: Invulnerable Moonsilver Carapace
summary: Capstone of the Defensive III tree; floods the Lunar's body in a fluid moonsilver carapace, adding a huge, perfect soak bonus for the turn at a crippling Essence cost and a Dexterity/Perception penalty.
description: By activating this Charm, the Lunar shields herself in a carapace of moonsilver, which appears to flow out of her pores to completely cover her body in shimmering plates. There are no gaps or weak points in this armor, which glistens fluidly as the Lunar moves. Though appearing to be liquid, the Invulnerable Moonsilver Carapace is invulnerable to any form of attack. It adds 15B/15L to the Lunar's soak until the end of the turn. This soak stacks with armor and cannot be circumvented by any stratagem, Charm or sorcery (this is a perfect effect) and is not armor for the purposes of Charms that do not work with armor. Its Essence cost is, however, crippling. During turns when the Invulnerable Moonsilver Carapace is activated, the Lunar suffers a -3 penalty to her Dexterity and Perception, though these cannot reduce the Attributes below 1.
prerequisiteText: Limb-Shielding Growth, Scales of the Dragon

name: Beast Instinct Method
summary: Root of the Survival and Healing I/II trees; lets a Lunar purchase bonus dice on Survival rolls up to his unmodified Wits.
description: A Lunar's ties to the wild allow him to survive in conditions where others would suffer great hardship. By using this Charm, the Lunar taps into his bestial nature, using instinct and cunning rather than rational thought to guide his actions. When attempting any form of Survival roll that involves Wits, the Lunar's player may purchase additional dice up to his character's unmodified Wits score.

name: Whale-Breath Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar hold his breath for Stamina x 10 minutes and survive underwater, in poison gas, or where there is no air at all, though he cannot speak while it is active.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar replicates the breath control of a diving whale and need not breathe for a considerable period of time (Stamina x 10 minutes). The Lunar can survive underwater, in poison gas, or where there's no air at all. However, the Lunar cannot speak without compromising the Charm -- doing so requires him to expel air from his lungs. The Lunar may speak a few words, perhaps a short sentence, but if he does so, the duration of the Charm decreases to one minute. If he speaks again, the duration decreases to five turns. A third attempt at speech or any form of longer communication cancels the Charm. As part of activating the Charm, the Lunar must take a deep breath and so cannot simply reactivate it in hostile conditions.

name: Gill-Breathing Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar grow gills so he can breathe underwater as well as in air for the rest of the day; can be re-triggered for 5 motes to keep the gills indefinitely.
description: By activating this Charm, the Lunar manipulates his body to form gills. This allows him to breathe as well in water as in air for the rest of the day. A character existing underwater may simply commit 5 motes to keep gills indefinitely.

name: Sealskin Endurance
summary: Lets a Lunar grow a protective layer (blubber, thick fur, etc.) that lets him exist in relative comfort in the coldest conditions, immune to hypothermia, frostbite, immersion, and snow blindness.
description: By activating this Charm, the Lunar protects himself from cold conditions. The exact method differs from Lunar to Lunar -- some may grow a layer of blubber, others a pelt of warm fur -- but the effects are the same. For the duration of the Charm, the Lunar can exist in relative comfort even in the coldest conditions. He does not suffer from hypothermia, frostbite or immersion, nor does he suffer the effects of snow blindness. He is not, however, protected from the harshest rigors of the Elemental Poles, nor from magically conjured cold.

name: Heat Adapting Method
summary: The opposite of Sealskin Endurance; makes the Lunar's body lean and efficient for warm environments, immune to heatstroke, sand blindness, blistering and sunburn.
description: This Charm has the opposite effect of Sealskin Endurance, resulting in a lean, sleek Lunar adapted to the rigors of warm environments. His body becomes highly efficient at conserving water and adept at radiating excess heat without the need for sweating. For the duration of the Charm, the Lunar can exist in relative comfort in even the warmest conditions. He does not suffer heatstroke or sand blindness, nor does his skin blister and burn after exposure to the sun. The Heat Adapting Method does not protect the Lunar from the effects of fire.

name: Fire-Walking Prana
summary: Lets a Lunar walk through flames and across burning coals without suffering ill effects for a short time, adding his Essence to his soak against magical fire and resisting smoke inhalation and overheating.
description: By means of this Charm, the Lunar can -- for a short time -- resist the effects of fire. He may walk through flames and across burning coals without suffering ill effects. He is not, however, immune to the effects of prolonged heat. The character adds his Essence to his soak against magical fire. While under the protection of this Charm, the character is also immune to the effects of smoke inhalation and to overheating caused by exposure to flames.

name: Unerring Den-Finding Sense
summary: Lets a Lunar unerringly find shelter suited to the environment for himself and a number of associates via a Perception + Survival roll, though it only guarantees shelter, not food or firewood.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can unerringly find shelter for himself and a number of associates. The exact sort of shelter will depend on the environment -- in rocky terrain, the Lunar's senses may lead him to a cave or cleft, while, in a forest, he may divine a hollow tree of suitable size. The Lunar's player makes a Perception + Survival roll, each success indicating capacity for one person, irrespective of the environmental conditions. However, this protection merely shields the characters from the elements -- it does not guarantee there be firewood or food in the vicinity.

name: Food-Scenting Method
summary: Lets a Lunar never go hungry in hospitable terrain by finding food for himself and, with a Perception + Survival roll, for a number of companions equal to his successes.
description: By using this Charm, a Lunar will never go hungry. If he is traveling during the day in hospitable terrain, the Lunar is guaranteed to find enough nuts, berries, ants and fungi to keep him well fed. If he actively forages for food, the Lunar gathers sufficient food to feed a number of people equal to his Perception + Survival, though doing so will take approximately an hour of his time. In harsher environments, the Lunar is still able to feed himself, though the Storyteller may wish the Lunar's player to roll his character's Perception + Survival, perhaps even at an increased difficulty level, to determine how many people he can feed. In no case should the difficulty increase above 3 unless the Lunar is stranded on pack ice, in the midst of a vast loose-sand desert, or in some other wildly hostile environment.

name: Water-Providing Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar find sufficient water for his own needs for a day, and, with a Perception + Survival roll, gather enough water for a number of other people even under harsh conditions.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can find sufficient water to meet his needs for a day. This moisture may be from concealed springs, condensation on leaves or the pulp of vegetation. Lunars in dire straits have gathered the film of moisture from around individual grains of sand, so sensitive are their tongues. If he may gather sufficient moisture to meet the needs of a number of people (including the Lunar), though harsh conditions may require his player to roll against a difficulty depending on the circumstances, each success indicating sufficient water for a person. Finding water takes 30 minutes per person, and as with the Food-Scenting Method above, the difficulty to find water where should never rise above 3.

name: Wolf Endurance Method
summary: Root of the Survival and Healing II tree's upper branch; lets a Lunar's body run on Essence instead of food, drink and rest for a number of weeks equal to his Stamina, at a cost of temporary Attribute loss thereafter.
description: Many wild beasts can go for days without nourishment, and the Wolf Endurance Method allows the Lunar Exalted to do likewise. On a day that the Charm is active, the Lunar does not need to eat or drink and does not suffer any hunger pangs. Unfortunately, while Essence can support the body for a short while, it is very inefficient at powering the metabolism of an Exalted. As a result, the Wolf Endurance Method can be used for a number of weeks equal to the character's Stamina. After that point, the Lunar may temporarily loose a point of Strength or Stamina for each additional week. Attribute points lost in this manner cannot be recovered until the Charm is discontinued and the character has had several square and nutritious meals.

name: Bear Sleep Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar hibernate for up to several months, needing neither food nor drink, but risking his Stamina and eventually death if woken early or deprived of shelter.
description: By activating this Charm, the Lunar can place himself in a deep sleep, during which time he need not eat and drink. Instead, Essence and body fat reserves sustain the Lunar. The Lunar may place himself in this hibernation for a number of months up to his Stamina score, paying 3 motes of Essence and 1 point of temporary Stamina to maintain his body during this time. However long he sleeps, the Lunar will be ravenous upon waking. The Lunar must have a solid meal within 24 hours of waking, or else, he loses an additional point of Stamina each day until he does. The Wolf Endurance Method cannot offset this Stamina loss -- after hibernating, the Lunar is beyond mere hunger. If his Stamina declines to 0, the Lunar dies. Every day after waking during which he eats properly allows the character to recover one point of Stamina (including the one spent when activating the Charm).

name: Fortitude of the Aurochs
summary: Lets a Lunar work for 24 hours without worry of fatigue, ignoring fatigue from Charms, sorcery, other effects, labor, and wearing armor, though not eliminating penalties already active before it was invoked.
description: Constant activity places a great strain on the body, and even Exalts become fatigued after prolonged activity. By using Fortitude of the Aurochs, a Lunar can reinvigorate his body with Essence, manipulating the muscles and blood of his body to allow him to remain active. With this Charm in use, a Lunar can work for 24 hours without worry of fatigue. He does not become fatigued as a result of Charms, sorcery or other effects. Fortitude of the Aurochs does not eliminate any penalties already in effect as a result of fatigue, nor does it negate the need for sleep, only weariness from labor. Fortitude of the Aurochs also negates the need to make fatigue rolls for wearing armor, irrespective of environmental conditions.

name: Ever-Waking Method
summary: Lets a Lunar reinvigorate his limbs with Essence to go 24 hours without sleep and suffer no penalties, though the fatigue symptoms are still visible; not recommended for extended use since it costs Willpower daily and long recovery afterward.
description: By using Essence to reinvigorate his limbs, a Lunar can go for 24 hours without sleep and suffer no penalties. He remains fully alert during this time and can keep acting, though the Charm does nothing to alleviate the symptoms of fatigue. The character can activate this Charm every day, but doing so for a prolonged period of time is not recommended -- after a number of days equal to the character's Stamina, Essence alone is not sufficient to reinvigorate the Lunar. Each day thereafter, he must also spend a temporary Willpower, which he cannot recover without a prolonged period of sleep. After the Charm is discontinued, the Lunar must sleep for six hours for each day he was awake.

name: Pain-Numbing Prana
summary: Root of the Survival and Healing III tree; lets a Lunar suppress bashing wound penalties for a number of turns equal to twice his Stamina + Endurance, though lethal/aggravated penalties and incapacitation from injury still apply.
description: By utilizing this Charm, a Lunar can suppress superficial feelings of pain for a short period of time, overriding his nervous system. The duration of this Charm is equal in turns to twice the Lunar's Stamina + Endurance, during which time he may ignore any wound penalties imposed by bashing damage. However, he still suffers the effects of lethal and aggravated damage and is still rendered unconscious if his wounds (of any type) reach incapacitated.

name: Will of the Stoic Warrior
summary: Lets a Lunar ignore wound penalties from moderate to severe pain (including bashing, lethal, and severe trauma), though aggravated-damage penalties still apply and incapacitation from any wound type still knocks him out.
description: Will of the Stoic Warrior allows the Lunar to suppress moderate to severe pain, such as the result of severe trauma, allowing him to ignore the dice pool penalties imposed by bashing or lethal damage. However, he still suffers the penalties imposed by aggravated damage and is still rendered unconscious if his wounds (of any type) reach incapacitated. The effects of this Charm last for a number of turns equal to the Exalt's Stamina + Endurance.

name: Luna's Fortitude
summary: Capstone of the Survival and Healing III tree; lets a Lunar ignore all wound penalties entirely for as long as he sustains the Charm each turn, but all deferred wound effects hit at once (potentially fatally) when it ends.
description: By calling on Luna's Fortitude, a Lunar ignores all wounds, period. Any wounds already present remain, and he may sustain new ones, but he suffers no action penalties while the Charm is in effect and is not rendered unconscious (or killed) no matter how far past incapacitated his injuries would take him. A character may sustain use of this Charm for a number of turns equal to his Stamina but must pay for the Charm in each turn. When the Charm ends, all wound effects immediately come into play; if the Lunar has suffered more points of lethal damage than he has health levels (including the health levels below Incapacitated provided by his Stamina), he dies immediately.

name: Infection-Resisting Method
summary: Root of the Survival and Healing IV tree; lets a Lunar convert Stamina dice into automatic successes when resisting disease or infection, though it does nothing to cure an existing infection.
description: Though diseases and infections are rarely a problem for the Exalted, the harsh lifestyles of the Lunar Exalted expose them to a wide range of contagions, and so, they have learned to use Essence to fortify their metabolisms. When making a roll to resist disease or infection, the Lunar's player may activate this Charm to convert the Lunar's Stamina dice into automatic successes. He may convert as many successes as he has points as the Lunar has of Stamina. The Infection-Resisting Method only helps to avoid disease; it does not resist or to cure disease once the Lunar has become infected.

name: Disease Purging Essence
summary: Lets a Lunar purge his own body of even the foulest plagues and infections by converting Stamina dice into automatic successes on a Stamina + Endurance roll to overcome an infected wound or disease.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar Exalted can purge his body of even the foulest plagues and infections. When rolling Stamina + Endurance to determine if the Lunar can overcome an infected wound or a disease, the Lunar's player can purchase automatic dice up to the value of the character's Stamina Attribute.

name: Bruise-Relief Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar spend Essence to heal his own bashing damage on the spot, 1 mote per health level per point of Stamina, leaving no scars and usable even while unconscious.
description: The minor contusions represented by bashing damage are of almost negligible concern to a Lunar Exalted, who, by exploiting his shapechanging abilities, can quickly repair bruises, sprains and related injuries. By expending Essence to repair this damage, the Exalt can cause his malleable flesh to repair damage. For every mote spent, the Exalt may remove one health level of bashing damage per point of Stamina, at a cost of 1 mote of Essence per health level. The Lunar does not have to repair all of his lethal damage with this Charm -- he may leave some to heal naturally. To an observer, bruises and other superficial injuries simply fade away to leave unblemished skin. Characters may activate this Charm even if unconscious.
reviewFlags: The rate/cost sentence in the source ('For every mote spent, the Exalt may remove one health level of bashing damage per point of Stamina, at a cost of 1 mote of Essence per health level') reads redundantly; paraphrased faithfully as written, but flagged here as possibly reflecting an OCR-adjacent print/layout artifact rather than a genuine rules ambiguity -- worth a second look before promotion.

name: Halting the Scarlet Flow
summary: Lets a Lunar reflexively heal his own lethal damage into bashing damage, 2 motes per health level converted, and automatically close bleeding wounds; works even while unconscious or dying.
description: By exploiting his shapeshifting abilities, a Lunar Exalted is quickly able to deal with cuts and other wounds, causing the flesh around gashes to flow together and broken bones to magically reknit. The Exalt may spend 2 motes to transform a level of lethal damage into bashing damage. In addition, if even one health level is healed, any bleeding wounds automatically close, preventing the loss of further health levels. The Lunar does not have to repair all of his lethal damage with this Charm -- he may leave some to heal naturally. Observers will see the blood flow cease, wounds knit together and swelling subside. Wounds healed with this Charm do not scar. Characters may activate this Charm even if unconscious and dying of mortal injury but cannot activate it if they are actually dead.

name: Lick Wound
summary: Lets a Lunar lick or breathe on an ally's wounds to lend the ally his own Essence and Stamina, boosting the ally's rolls or purchased dice against disease or infection.
description: Using this Charm while licking a subject's wounds or breathing vapors into her face, allows the Lunar to use his own Essence to fortify an ally's resistance to infection. The player may purchase dice up to his character's Stamina and add them to the subject's efforts to resist infection or disease, or her player's rolls to overcome illness or sickness.

name: Mother's Touch
summary: Capstone of the Survival and Healing IV tree; lets a Lunar heal an ally's bashing and lethal wounds by touch, downgrade lethal to bashing, close bleeding, and even downgrade aggravated damage to lethal at a Willpower cost, up to his Stamina in levels per use.
description: By infusing his hands with Essence and touching a subject's wounds, a Lunar is able to heal or alleviate those wounds. These healing hands can remove bashing damage and transform lethal wounds into bashing. Mother's Touch also closes bleeding wounds, preventing the loss of additional health levels healed costs 2 motes of Essence, while each level of lethal transformed costs 3 motes. Mother's Touch can be used to transform aggravated damage (into lethal), but each health level removed costs 3 motes and a temporary Willpower point. With each use of Mother's Touch, the Lunar may transform/cure as many levels of damage as he has points of Stamina.
cost: 2 or 3 motes per health level, or 3 motes plus 1 Willpower per health level
prerequisiteText: Halting the Scarlet Flow, Lick Wound

name: Sense-Sharpening Change
summary: Root of the Perception I tree; heightens all of the Lunar's senses beyond normal humans for a scene, adding bonus dice to Perception rolls up to his Perception dots, though it only enhances mortal senses.
description: Using this Charm, the Lunar can heighten all of his senses beyond those of normal humans. His ears grow to better hear sound, his nostrils flare to enhance his ability to smell, and his eyes grow and dilate to enhance his sight -- he can even taste individual ingredients in a meal and feel the slightest wind on his skin. For the duration of the Charm, the Lunar's player adds bonus dice equal to the amount of Essence spent to Perception rolls. He may not increase the character's pool by more dice through this Charm than the Lunar has dots of Perception. This enhancement, though powered by Essence, does not grant the character supernatural powers -- it merely enhances his mortal senses.

name: Heightened (Sense) Method
summary: Actually three separate Charms (sight; hearing and touch; smell and taste) that automatically succeed the Lunar's Perception dice on rolls using the honed sense, purchased and capped separately per sense group.
description: This Charm is actually three different Charms, one each for sight, for scent and for hearing and touch. Through it, the Lunar can hone his senses far beyond those of most animals. When making a Perception test with the heightened sense, the Lunar's Perception dice are automatically successes, and the Lunar's player need only roll the character's Ability dice (usually Awareness or Survival). Charms that reduce successes in Perception tests affect these automatic successes normally. The Charm must be purchased separately for each of the three sense groups and only provides a bonus when used in conjunction with that sense group. A Lunar may use a maximum of two Heightened (Sense) Charms at any time. If he wishes to enhance a third, he must cease using the Charm on one of the already-heightened senses. Heightened (Sense) Method Charms may not be used at the same time as the Sense-Sharpening Change or any other Charm that boosts the Lunar's Perception, though they may be used in conjunction with sense-enhancing Charms that do not directly enhance the Perception Trait, such as Night Is Day.

name: Ever-Wary Fox Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar automatically gain a reflexive Perception + Awareness roll to avoid being ambushed if he has sufficient Essence, with bonus dice equal to his Perception.
description: Lunars are ever aware of their environments and, thus, are very difficult to ambush. When the character is attacked from surprise, the Lunar may choose to activate this Charm automatically if the character has sufficient Essence to power it. When it does activate, the Lunar's player's reflexive Perception + Awareness roll to avoid being ambushed gains a number of bonus dice equal to the Lunar's Perception.

name: Sense-Borrowing Method
summary: Lets a Lunar attach his senses to another human or animal within a mile per point of Essence, seeing entirely through the subject's senses at a +2 difficulty to his own reflexive actions.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can attach his senses to those of another human or an animal. The Lunar must touch the target when activating the Charm, but once it is functioning, the target may travel up to a mile from the Lunar per point of the Exalt's permanent Essence and still be a source of sensory information. If the subject is willing, no roll is required to activate the Charm. Otherwise, the Lunar's player must make a Wits + Awareness roll, with a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. Animals of the Lunar's totem species are automatically willing, while others are not unless charmed or befriended. To succeed, the Lunar's player must roll a number of successes equal to or exceeding the target's Essence. Otherwise, the Charm fails, and if the target is a magically aware creature, he knows the Lunar or other supernatural beasts attempted to use a Charm on him. While the Charm is active, the Lunar senses everything his subject does. For all intents and purposes, the subject becomes the Lunar's eyes and ears. The Lunar has some semblance of his own senses, but borrowed senses dominate his perceptions. Any actions taken by the Lunar while the Sense-Borrowing Method is being used -- including reflexive actions -- are at +2 difficulty. As a consequence, most Lunars simply meditate while using the Charm. If either the Lunar or his subject sustain an injury (at least one health level of damage), the Charm ends. This Charm gives the Lunar no control over the creature, he simply shares its senses.

name: Observed Prey Instinct
summary: Lets a Lunar automatically know when he is being watched by normal senses or magic, with a reflexive Perception + Awareness roll to learn how many observers and where they are.
description: This reflexive Charm allows a Lunar to know if he is being watched, either by normal senses or magic. It activates automatically if the Lunar comes under sustained observation -- a casual glance or a flirtatious look are not enough to trigger it. The Charm guides his perceptions to gather further information, allowing a reflexive Perception + Awareness roll. The number of successes determines the information gathered. A single success merely confirms that the Lunar is being observed, while additional successes will pinpoint the number and direction of observers (one per success). A Lunar observed by magical means will know the viewpoint from which he is being watched but not the actual location of the observer.

name: Weather-Scenting Method
summary: Lets a Lunar track and predict local weather using Wits + Survival, purchasing knowledge of conditions within a 10-mile radius or of future conditions up to several days out.
description: Lunars with this Charm can track and predict the weather, using Essence to build on and extend their natural perceptions. The number of successes from a Wits + Survival roll determines the scope of information a Lunar can divine. Each success garners him either knowledge of conditions within a 10-mile radius or for the next day (cumulative). A Lunar may purchase information on both area and time, but he must do so in as even a manner as possible. For example, a Lunar who gets 4 successes cannot purchase information on a 40-mile radius for 4 days in advance, but rather learns about a 20-mile radius for two days in advance. If there are an odd number of successes, the Lunar's player may choose which aspect has the additional die. The Weather-Scenting Method may not be used to predict future conditions under the influence of magic, though it may be used to gather information on the prevailing conditions when the Charm is activated.

name: Unerring Earth Direction Sense
summary: Lets a Lunar instinctively know the direction of the Imperial Mountain from anywhere, and, with a Wits + Awareness roll, pinpoint his own location with increasing precision.
description: After activating this Charm, the Lunar instinctively knows the direction of the Imperial Mountain. This works irrespective of the Lunar's situation -- it is as effective inside a building or underground as it is in plains or forest -- and works as well in darkness as in daylight. If the Lunar simply desires to know the direction of the Imperial Mountain, no roll is required. However, he may also use this Charm to identify his location, though this requires a Wits + Awareness roll, the number of successes indicating the precision of the information. One success gives him little more than what he already knows, three successes allows him to narrow his location down to the city or district, and five or more let him know precisely where he stands.

name: Wyld-Sensing Instincts
summary: Lets a Lunar reflexively sense encroaching Wyld warping before it takes hold, giving him and his associates minutes to escape or take shelter depending on how many successes he rolls.
description: Having existed on the edge of the world, Lunar Exalted are ever watchful for the warping effects of the Wyld. Though their nature and their tattoos protect them from its deforming effects, their associates and non-Lunar kin are less fortunate, and their gear is often vulnerable as well. Provided the Lunar has sufficient motes available, Wyld-Sensing Instincts activates reflexively to alert the Lunar when this malign change occurs. Immediately after it does, the Lunar's player must make a (non-reflexive) Perception + Survival roll. The number of successes indicates the amount of time the Lunar has to act before changes occur. One success gives the Lunar a few turns to escape the transformations, while three successes indicates he has several minutes to reach safety. Five or more successes indicates that, while the chaos is not yet approaching dangerous levels, the Lunar has as much as 30 minutes to seek refuge -- or to otherwise protect -- his associates.

name: Moonsilver-Scenting Sense
summary: Lets a Lunar scent moonsilver deposits or unattuned moonsilver weapons in the region via a Wits + Awareness roll, with more successes revealing distance, quality, and concealment attempts.
description: The Moonsilver-Scenting Sense hones the Lunar's olfactory nerves, allowing her to scent deposits of moonsilver or moonsilver weapons not attuned to a Lunar in the surrounding lands. The Lunar's player must make a Wits + Awareness roll, the number of successes determining what -- if anything -- the character learns of the region. One success allows the Lunar to ascertain whether there is any moonsilver within a number of miles equal to the Lunar's Perception + Essence. Three successes also provide direction and approximate distance. Five or more successes allow the Lunar to judge the quality and condition (e.g., concealed by Dragon-Blooded machinations) of the deposits or items. The Lunar's player may make one roll for every 10 minutes that the Charm is active.

name: Wyld Object Appraisal Method
summary: Lets a Lunar inspect an item touched by the Wyld and determine its original, uncorrupted form and whether it will retain its present form if returned to Creation.
description: Although all Exalted can attempt to discern if something is safe to remove from the Wyld and will retain its form if removed, this ability is far from certain. With the use of this Charm, a Lunar can absolutely tell what the original form of a creation of the Wyld was, whether it will be safe to remove it from Creation and whether or not it will retain its present form when removed. The Lunar can usually inspect only a single item through the use of this Charm, although a number of similar small items could be checked at the same time.

name: Resisting the Lure of Madness
summary: Lets a Lunar become immune to Wyld addiction for a lunar month; addicted characters do not need to worry about addictive behavior or relapse while it persists but are not cured.
description: A character who activates this Charm is immune to Wyld addiction while the Charm's effects persist. Characters addicted to the Wyld do not have to worry about addictive behavior or relapse while the Charm continues, but those not addicted will not become so while under the magic's sway.

name: Harmony With Reality Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar force a piece of Wyld-touched material (up to 50 pounds per point of Essence) to permanently become part of Creation, forcing it to whatever improbable or weird form results, unlike a Solar's ability to shape it as desired.
description: A Lunar skilled in the ways of the Wyld can force his will upon it, causing it to accede to his whims. While he cannot create exactly what is desired, as a Solar can, he can force the things he touches to retain their form and function when returned to Creation, no matter how improbable or weird, in essence, he forces that part of the Wyld to become part of Creation. This Charm cannot affect more than 50 pounds of material per point of the character's permanent Essence.
cost: 10 motes plus 1 additional mote per pound of material, 1 Willpower
prerequisiteText: Wyld Object Appraisal Method, Wondrous Lunar Transformation

name: Ritual of Lunar Stability
summary: Capstone of the Perception I tree; lets a Lunar mark out a protected area around himself with his scent and presence, reducing local Wyld intensity by a level per three successes for months equal to his permanent Essence.
description: There are many places on the edges of Creation that are kept safe only through the use of ancient rituals, secret pacts or powerful sorceries. While this Charm cannot replace these powers, it can provide sanctuary from the effects of the Wyld for a time. The use of this Charm requires that the Lunar first pace out the area he wishes to protect, encircling it with her scent and presence; this area can be no larger than a number of square miles equal to her permanent Essence. Once this is done, she sees the Charm, and her player rolls Wits + Lore. For every three successes scored, the level of the Wyld in the protected area is reduced by one (so if she scored six successes, she would reduce an area of Deep Wyld down in intensity to be equivalent to Bordermarches). This effect lasts a number of weeks equal to her permanent Essence.
duration: A number of lunar months equal to permanent Essence

name: Fish-Eye Technique
summary: Root of the Perception II tree (aliased under the Heightened Sight Method); gives the Lunar 360-degree vision, immune to being caught unawares by visible attacks, at the cost of +1 difficulty to spot fine details.
description: By means of this Charm, a Lunar modifies the shape and the nature of his eyes. He gains 360-degree vision and, as a result, is aware of actions all around him and does not suffer penalties for being caught unawares by visible attacks. However, comprehending such a vista forces the Lunar to focus on the 'big picture' rather than the details and, as a result, increases by 1 the difficulty of any Perception rolls involving spotting details.
prerequisiteText: Heightened (Sense) Method (sight aspect, shown in the tree diagram as 'Heightened Sight Method')

name: Night Is Day
summary: Lets a Lunar see perfectly in low-light conditions as though it were daylight, giving up a bit of color vision as a partial trade-off, manifesting as flashing, cat-like eyes.
