description: Using this Charm, a Lunar alters his eyes to allow him to see perfectly in low-light conditions, though he treats nighttime conditions as daylight, he is partially colorblind (+1 difficulty to Perception rolls in normally lit conditions) for the duration of the Charm. Night Is Day does not allow the Lunar to see in absolute darkness -- there must be some light, even if just a twinkle, for the Lunar's eyes to exploit. The Charm manifests by giving the Lunar flashing, cat-like eyes while it is active.
prerequisiteText: Heightened (Sense) Method (sight aspect, shown in the tree diagram as 'Heightened Sight Method')

name: Perceiving the Hidden World
summary: Capstone of the Perception II tree; lets a Lunar see in perfect darkness by perceiving heat and other light forms invisible to humans, at the cost of +2 difficulty to fine-detail Perception rolls.
description: Some animals can see light incomprehensible to humans, most often the spectral glows of heat and cold. Using this Charm, a Lunar can do likewise, allowing him to perceive radiated heat and other forms of light normally beyond his experience. This allows him to see in perfect darkness, though his ability to distinguish detail is greatly impaired (+2 difficulty to all Perception rolls involving fine detail).

name: Rabbit Ear Method
summary: Root branch of the Perception III tree (aliased under Heightened Hearing & Touch Method); enlarges the Lunar's ears to track others in his vicinity via a Perception + Awareness roll, with more successes revealing direction, range, and activity.
description: Using this Charm -- which, in any form, causes his ears to enlarge and resemble those of a rabbit or stiff-eared dog -- a Lunar can use his enhanced hearing to keep track of others in his immediate vicinity without needing to have them in sight. He is dimly aware of others' presence and may reach with his senses to pinpoint them and gather extra information. Doing so requires a Perception + Awareness roll, difficulty 1 in wilderness conditions, 2 in the streets of a town and 3 inside a structure. One success indicates that the Lunar is aware of those around him, but only in a general sense, while three successes provide him with an approximate direction and range to each. Five or more successes allow provide information on their activities, equipment carried and identities. The Lunar may use this Charm to track a number of others equal to (his Essence x 5) and perceive them out to (his Perception x 100) yards. Unless concealed by Charms, those closest to the Lunar are revealed first, and those furthest from him last. A Storyteller may, at his discretion, identify more distant targets first if they are somehow 'broadcasting' their presence by making lots of noise.
prerequisiteText: Heightened (Sense) Method (hearing/touch aspect, shown in the tree diagram as 'Heightened Hearing & Touch Method')

name: Comprehending Ears Meditation
summary: Lets a Lunar understand any spoken human language or dialect (with increasing fluency at more successes) via a Wits + Linguistics roll, though it grants no ability to speak the tongue or understand nonverbal communication.
description: This Charm allows a Lunar to understand -- in general terms if not the exact meaning of words -- any language spoken in his presence. The Lunar's player must roll Wits + Linguistics, with the number of successes indicating the level of comprehension. One success indicates he can get the general gist of what's being said, while three successes afford solid comprehension. Five or more successes allow the Lunar to discern nuances of what has been said, be they insults or flattery. Comprehending Ears Meditation does not allow the Lunar to speak a foreign tongue. Comprehending Ears Meditation does not allow the Lunar to understand nonverbal communication.
prerequisiteText: Heightened (Sense) Method (hearing/touch aspect, shown in the tree diagram as 'Heightened Hearing & Touch Method')

name: Calls of the Human Prey
summary: Lets a Lunar who has eaten a victim's Heart's Blood understand and speak any language or dialect known by that person via a Wits + Linguistics roll, with fluency scaling with successes, though it carries a distinct accent.
description: By activating this Charm, a Lunar can attempt to both understand and speak any language or dialect known by people he has consumed. The Lunar's player makes a Wits + Linguistics roll when the Charm activates. The difficulty is 5 - (the number of people who spoke the language the Lunar has eaten the heart's blood of). The number of successes on the roll determines the Lunar's level of comprehension and fluency. One success indicates linguistic capabilities comparable with a young child, while three successes denote average adult abilities. Five or more successes grant the skills of a poet. Calls of the Human Prey does not allow the Lunar to read or write the language, nor does it make her a perfect mimic. If the Lunar has eaten only a few victims fluent in a single language, his voice may possess a distinct accent that damages his ability to socialize with those who dislike his dialect.

name: Feral Ears Metamorphosis
summary: Lets a Lunar understand and communicate in general terms with any animal in his presence via a Wits + Linguistics roll, using the same comprehension scale as Comprehending Ears Meditation but for beasts instead of people.
description: This Charm allows a Lunar to understand and communicate with -- in general if not in precise terms -- any animals in his presence. It functions as per the Comprehending Ears Meditation, save with regard to its subjects. The Lunar's player makes a Wits + Linguistics roll when the Lunar activates the Charm, with a difficulty of 5 - (the number of beasts of that species the Lunar has eaten the heart's blood of). The Lunar need only get one success in most cases, as valid animals are not generally articulate. However, if the animal is a complex thinker normally unable to communicate, then more successes may be relevant. A Lunar using this Charm can automatically understand the language of his totem animal form (no roll needed).

name: Seeing Without Looking
summary: Capstone of the Perception III tree; lets a Lunar build a detailed mental picture of his surroundings by echoic hearing alone over five turns, letting him fight and identify hidden things while functionally blind.
description: By focusing his hearing, a Lunar can build a mental picture of the surrounding area. Unlike the Rabbit Ear Method, which only tracks individuals, Seeing Without Looking also allows the Lunar to build up an idea of the objects and materials that make up the environs by analyzing subtle alterations in the sound of echoes. Analyzing the sounds he hears takes the Lunar five turns, during which time he may move about at a walking pace but cannot take any other actions. If he does, the Charm fails. After five turns have elapsed, the Exalt's player makes a Perception + Awareness roll. The number of successes on this roll determines the quality and the range to which the sense applies. One success indicates that the Lunar has a general picture of the surroundings, including the position of people, beasts and major obstacles. However, he knows little about their composition and size and cannot tell the difference between two small objects placed close together. Three successes let the Lunar refine his search, allowing him to identify the materials and giving him a finer 'resolution' in his sense. Five or more successes allow the Lunar to identify most details in his immediate area, save those that can only be gleaned by sight (such as color). With five successes, the Lunar can also identify hidden people and items in the vicinity, even if Charms were used as part of the concealment process. The Lunar's mental picture extends a number of yards equal to (the number of successes on the Perception roll x 5). Provided he maintains the Charm and carries out no actions other than walking, the mental image remains constant. However, as soon as he carries out any action or ceases to spend Essence, the picture 'locks' though the Lunar may still act on the details for the remainder of the scene. Thus, a Lunar who wishes to fight blind will need to use this Charm to build up a picture of his surroundings and Rabbit Ear Method to sense his foes. However, such a Lunar might be deceived by sliding walls, silently opening pits or other changes that make the static picture of his environment obsolete.

name: Blood-Kin Sense
summary: Root branch of the Perception IV tree (aliased under Heightened Smell and Taste Method); lets a Lunar sense blood ties between individuals via a Perception + Awareness roll, with more successes revealing lineage details, especially potent if the Lunar tastes the target's blood.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can immediately sense the blood ties between other individuals. A Lunar's player may make a Perception + Awareness roll when the character targets the Blood-Kin Sense on an individual. If the player gets at least one success, the Lunar knows if the person is related to someone else the Lunar is familiar with, while three successes give some indication of the relationship. Five or more allow the Lunar to sense firm details of the subject's lineage, including a capsule history of the being's ancestor's physical abilities for a number of generations back equal to the Lunar's Essence. The Blood-Kin Sense assumes the Lunar is using scent to study his subject. If the Lunar tastes the target's blood, his player gains three bonus dice for the roll.
prerequisiteText: Heightened (Sense) Method (smell/taste aspect, shown in the tree diagram as 'Heightened Smell and Taste Method')

name: Blood on the Wind
summary: Lets a Lunar track a person or animal across almost any terrain by scent via a Perception + Survival roll, needing only one success to follow mundane prey and gaining automatic tracking successes against other supernatural trackers while in beastman form.
description: By means of the Charm, a Lunar can track an opponent (or opponents) through almost any terrain. To the Lunar, the trail is as clear on solid stone as it is in the woodlands or on soft ground. When making a tracking roll (Perception + Survival) for the character, her player need roll only a single success for the character to follow his mundane prey. Furthermore, if the Lunar is in beastman form when using this Charm, he is considered to be a supernatural tracker and has a number of automatic successes in the tracking contest against other supernatural trackers equal to his Essence.
prerequisiteText: Heightened (Sense) Method (smell/taste aspect, shown in the tree diagram as 'Heightened Smell and Taste Method')

name: Emotion-Revealing Scent
summary: Lets a Lunar sense a target's true emotional state by scent even through a calm facade, requiring no roll for a basic impression but a Perception + Investigation roll for deeper insight into the cause.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can sense the emotional state of her subject, even if there are no outward signs. Even if the target appears perfectly calm, his body scent will betray him, allowing the Lunar to clearly scent strong emotions such as fear, anger, hate and love. Doing this does not require a dice roll, though it does count as a dice action. The Charm does not, automatically divine the cause of this emotion or its focus. To divine a deeper understanding of the target, the Lunar's player must roll Perception + Investigation, the number of successes indicating the degree of information gathered. One success merely confirms the initial impression, while three successes denote the source, target or object causing the emotions. Five or more successes allow the Lunar to deduce the reason for the emotion.
prerequisiteText: Heightened (Sense) Method (smell/taste aspect, shown in the tree diagram as 'Heightened Smell and Taste Method')

name: Truth-Scenting Method
summary: Capstone of the Perception IV tree; lets a Lunar detect lies by scent, targeted or ambient, though it only detects outright falsehoods (not evasions) and judges truth by the speaker's own belief, not objective fact.
description: By observing subtle physical and chemical responses in his subject, a Lunar can determine whether a person in his presence is speaking the truth -- in which case, he may target the Charm at an individual -- in which case it works more automatically -- or he may use it more generally on a body of people. In this latter case, the Lunar's player must roll Perception + Investigation, the number of successes being the number of people the Exalt can successfully observe. The Truth-Scenting Method does not detect evasions or statements that twist the truth without actually being falsehoods. Furthermore, some 'truths' are subjective, and it is the target's view, not that of the perceiving Lunar, which determines this. For Example: if a subject says, 'I saw him do it,' when he saw no such thing, the Lunar can detect the lie. However, the Charm will not detect a lie if the subject states, 'No, Janek didn't pay me anything' (because Marcos did), as it is an evasion, not an outright lie.

name: Stealthy Fox Method
summary: Root of the Stealth tree; lets a Lunar call on feral instincts to add bonus dice, up to his Dexterity, to any Stealth roll for the rest of the scene.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can call on his feral instincts to enhance any attempts to hide or use stealth. By honing both his senses and his agility, the Lunar exploits all cover to the maximum possible extent, avoiding obstacles that might alert others to his presence, and moves in such a graceful manner as to avoid catching the attention of unwary observers. For the rest of the scene, when making a roll to move stealthily or to hide, the Lunar's player may add bonus dice up to the character's dots of Dexterity, at a cost of 2 motes per die.

name: Chameleon Skin Disguise
summary: Lets a Lunar mimic chameleon skin to convert dice up to his Dexterity into automatic successes on Stealth rolls while holding still, paying upkeep motes to re-adapt his camouflage whenever he moves.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can mimic the skin of the chameleon and becomes able to adjust the texture and color of his hide to better aid in concealment. For the rest of the scene, as long as the character stays still, he may convert a number of dice up to his Dexterity Attribute into automatic successes on a Stealth roll, at a cost of 2 motes per dot of Dexterity converted. If the character moves any distance, the Lunar must reflexively spend 2 motes at the end of the movement to adapt the camouflage to his new background; the Charm's benefits are negated until the character pays these 2 motes. The Chameleon Skin Disguise provides the Lunar with no advantage if he is clothed or armored.

name: Object-Concealing Method
summary: Lets a Lunar find or create a hiding place for an item via Wits + Survival, with the roll's successes setting the difficulty for anyone deliberately searching for it afterward.
description: The Object-Concealing Method allows a Lunar both to find a suitable place of concealment for an item and to enhance its protection against a deliberate search. The Lunar's player rolls Wits + Survival, difficulty 1 (higher in terrain that offers few hiding places), searching an area out to (his Wits x 10) yards. If he succeeds, the Lunar has found a place of concealment for the item, and the number of successes becomes the difficulty for others' Perception + Investigation rolls to find the object in a deliberate search; the object cannot be discovered by accident. It takes (10 minus the Lunar's Essence) turns to hide the item.

name: Ally Concealing Method
summary: Extends the Object-Concealing Method to hide other characters instead of items, at a cost per person concealed, though the Lunar cannot use it to hide himself and it breaks if the hidden ally attacks.
description: This Charm functions as per the Object-Concealing Method, save that the thing being hidden is another character rather than an item. The concealing effect remains active so long as the affected character stays calm and relatively still; attacking will disrupt the camouflage. A Lunar may conceal as many people at once as his Essence Trait, at a cost of 5 motes each. A Lunar cannot use Ally Concealing Method to hide himself. It takes (10 minus the Lunar's Essence) turns to find a place of concealment for each individual.

name: Traceless Passage Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar erase all signs of his passage and resting places for a day, blocking mundane trackers entirely and imposing a difficulty penalty equal to his Essence on magically aided trackers (except other Lunars).
description: Lunars are crafty in the ways of the wild, adept at following -- or hiding -- signs of passage. There are times, however, when a Lunar wishes to truly disappear, throwing even the craftiest pursuers off the scent. Traceless Passage Technique allows him to do so, concealing evidence of his passage and disguising anywhere he rested. Trackers without magical enhancements are unable to follow his trail while the Charm is active, and those with Charms or sorcery to aid their tracking suffer a difficulty modifier equal to the Lunar's Essence. Traceless Passage Technique does not provide any automatic successes against other Lunars attempting to track him.

name: Track-Sweeping Essence
summary: Capstone of the Stealth tree; extends the Traceless Passage Technique's trail-concealing benefits to the Lunar's companions, at a mote cost per person covered (including the Lunar himself, if desired).
description: Using this Charm, the Lunar can extend the benefits of Traceless Passage Technique to his companions, and his instincts help to guide their actions as well as his own. Enacting the Charm costs 4 motes, and each person encompassed in Track-Sweeping Essence costs an additional 2 motes; if the Lunar wants to conceal his own passage as well, he must pay for himself. The Lunar can conceal the passage of as many people as he has points of Essence.

name: Tale-Spinning Mastery
summary: Root of the Interaction and Knowledge I tree; lets a Lunar storyteller add bonus dice (up to his Charisma) to any storytelling roll while addressing an audience of five or more people per extra mote spent.
description: Lunar society has little in the way of a written tradition, instead preferring to pass information down orally, often through stories. A master storyteller knows how to use Essence and his shapeshifting powers to enhance the tale, adjusting his voice and actions to suit the audience. Normally the Charm affects five subjects, but for each additional mote spent the speaker can increase his audience by five more people (a Lunar with sufficient Essence can address a crowd this way, though it is an inefficient method). While the Charm is in effect, the Lunar's player can add bonus dice to any test involving storytelling, though the bonus may not exceed the character's Charisma. The Storyteller may increase the difficulty of the roll if the audience is hostile, disinclined to listen, or otherwise distracted, and the audience must be able to comprehend the Lunar's speech for the Charm to work.

name: Lore-Speaking Method
summary: Lets a Lunar enter a meditative trance to search his memories for lore or historical knowledge via Intelligence + Wits, extending the trance's duration to dig deeper into recollection.
description: Most Moons do not believe in writing; their history, traditions and knowledge are conveyed orally. By using Lore-Speaking Method, a Lunar can enter a meditative trance and search his memories for relevant information. The trance lasts a minimum of 30 minutes, though it may be extended if he wishes, providing the Lunar's player with additional time to search: at the end of the meditation, the Lunar's player makes an Intelligence + Wits roll, adding a bonus die for each additional 10 minutes the character spent in meditation, to a maximum bonus of his Intelligence. The difficulty depends on the nature of the information sought -- 1 for routine matters, 3 for more obscure lore, and 5 for esoteric knowledge the No Moons may have mentioned only in passing -- and the net successes determine the strength and clarity of the recollection. The Storyteller may keep the exact difficulty secret, instead telling the Lunar how sure he is of the memory. If the Lunar's player rolls no successes, or if the Exalt is interrupted before 30 minutes have elapsed, the Charm fails.

name: Divining the Hidden Truth
summary: Lets a Lunar undertake a Wyld-touched vision quest to seek knowledge beyond his ken via Perception + Lore, risking disorientation, bashing damage, or worse on a poor or botched roll.
description: Sometimes a Lunar has need of information he does not know. In routine matters, he can turn to the No Moons, who may be able to provide what he needs in return for a boon, but some information can only be acquired from outside sources. A civilized Lunar might trek into the Threshold or even the Realm proper in his quest for knowledge; those with closer ties to the Wyld instead seek knowledge from their ancestors and friendly spirits by means of a vision quest, entering a deep trance and letting his mind and spirit wander free -- perhaps aided by psychotropic fungi or the crushed essence of certain beetles -- with no guarantee of success, and no easy way to distinguish real insight from mere imagination. At the end of the quest, which lasts a number of hours equal to the Lunar's Essence, his player may ask a single question and roll Perception + Lore, at a difficulty depending on the nature of the information sought -- routine information requires only a single success, hidden knowledge obscured deliberately or otherwise requires at least three successes, and even five successes may not suffice for the deepest secrets. The Lunar may not count more successes than his permanent Essence Trait and must discard any extras. Failing the roll can have devastating effects: if the Lunar gets at least one success but not enough to succeed, he simply wakes none the wiser, but failure leaves the Lunar disoriented and forced to soak a number of dice of bashing damage equal to his Essence, while a botch leaves him catatonic for a number of days equal to his Essence and may also result in a derangement.

name: Lion Roar Method
summary: Lets a Lunar transform his voice into a deafening roar audible for a long distance, usable as a pseudo-weapon against a nearby target that costs the target a point of Perception on a failed resistance roll.
description: Using this Charm to expand his lungs and vocal cords, a Lunar can transform his normal voice into a formidable roar. Anything the Lunar says while the Charm is in effect is clearly audible to anyone within a number of yards equal to (the Lunar's Essence x 100) and to those with acute hearing for twice that distance. A Lunar can also use the Lion Roar Method as a pseudo-weapon by roaring at an individual within 10 yards; that individual must make a reflexive Stamina + Endurance roll at a difficulty equal to the Lunar's Perception. If the target fails, he temporarily loses a point of Perception and must attempt to resist further exposure at a worsened difficulty for the remainder of the scene.

name: Wind-Speaking Method
summary: Lets a Lunar whisper a short message on the wind to a known recipient at range, with more successes on a Wits + Linguistics roll reducing delivery time and extending range.
description: Winds circulate around the world, and while not as skilled as the Dragon-Blooded at manipulating the elements, some Lunars do know how to call upon the wind and use it to convey messages to their allies. Upon activating this Charm, the Lunar whispers a few words (his Essence score x 5 in words maximum) and names a recipient. The Exalt's player then rolls Wits + Linguistics; the difficulty of the roll depends on the range to the intended recipient -- difficulty 1 if within 1,000 yards, two successes required for up to a mile, and three or more successes to reach up to five miles. The recipient must be known to the Lunar and must have spoken to him at some point in the past. The target is the only person to hear the message -- sending messages to multiple recipients requires multiple invocations of the Charm. There may be a delay in delivery depending on the range; it takes one hour for the message to cross 600 miles. The Storyteller may require a Wits + Performance roll to determine the clarity of the message at its destination.

name: River of Words
summary: Capstone of the Interaction and Knowledge I tree; a more powerful Wind-Speaking Method with no range limit, longer and multi-recipient messages, and a much larger maximum audience.
description: A more powerful version of the Wind-Speaking Method, River of Words allows messages that are more complex, longer distance and multiple recipients. There is no range limitation to the message transmission, though there may be a delay in delivery dependent on the range; it takes one hour for the message to travel up to 600 miles. The maximum number of recipients for a River of Words communiqué is equal to the Lunar's Essence, and the maximum number of words each message may contain is (the Lunar's Essence x 10).

name: Emotion-Shaping Technique
summary: Root of the Interaction and Knowledge II tree; lets a Lunar subtly raise or lower one of a target's Virtues (never above 5 or below 1, and never past a 2-dot swing) via successes on a Manipulation + Presence roll.
description: The Emotion Shaping Technique enhances a Lunar's already considerable presence, using a combination of charisma, insight and timing to allow the Exalt to manipulate the emotional responses of his audience. The target must be capable of understanding the Exalt for the Charm to function correctly but need not be paying full attention to what is being said; the Lunar's words and the Charm work on the subconscious mind as much as on the conscious mind. The Lunar's player rolls Manipulation + Presence, and each success allows the Lunar to temporarily increase or decrease one of the target's Virtues by a point. This may not raise the Virtue above 5, nor lower it below 1 (even under the influence of this Charm, a paragon of valor will not become a sniveling coward), and a Virtue may not be altered by more than two -- even across two uses of the Charm. Two successes could be applied one each to two Virtues or two to one Virtue of one character and one to one Virtue of another. However, other Charms such as the Crowd-Inciting Method and Courage-Building Address are better able to manipulate the Virtues of large numbers of people; this Charm does not work on spirits of any sort.

name: Crowd-Inciting Method
summary: Extends the Emotion-Shaping Technique to lower the Temperance or Compassion of a whole crowd via Manipulation + Performance, at a difficulty that scales with crowd size.
description: In broad terms, the Crowd-Inciting Method follows the same principles as the Emotion-Shaping Technique but is better suited to influence large numbers of people, albeit in a restricted manner. The Lunar must be heard by the crowd, and his player rolls Manipulation + Performance against a difficulty dependent on the size of the crowd (+1 per 50 people or fraction thereof). If the roll succeeds, the player may spend Essence to temporarily reduce the Temperance or Compassion Virtue of the crowd to a maximum of 2 dots and not below 0 (meaning that if the Exalt has more than four successes, some are wasted, perhaps making it more amenable to suggestions). A failed roll has no effect, but a botch may result in the crowd turning on the speaker.

name: Crowd-Calming Pronouncement
summary: Mirror-image of the Crowd-Inciting Method that instead temporarily raises a crowd's Compassion or Temperance (up to 5), at a higher base cost and difficulty.
description: The Crowd-Calming Pronouncement functions in the same manner as the Crowd-Inciting Method, save that it allows the Lunar to temporarily increase the Compassion or Temperance of the crowd by up to 2 dots (but not above 5). The base Essence cost is higher than the Crowd-Inciting Method, and the difficulty is +1 per 30 people in the crowd -- it is harder for the Lunar to calm a mob than to stir one into action. A failed roll has no effect, but a botch may result in the Lunar turning on the speaker.

name: Courage-Building Address
summary: Lets a Lunar deliver an inspirational pre-battle speech that temporarily raises troops' Valor via a Manipulation + Performance roll, scaling with the size of the addressed force.
description: In battle, numbers are rarely the deciding factor. Instead, troop quality is often the key, and courage is the cornerstone of that quality. By means of the Courage-Building Address, a Lunar can instill a sense of bravery in his troops, increasing their Valor Virtue for the duration of the battle (requiring at least four minutes) by means of an inspirational speech. While the Lunar makes the speech, his player must make a Manipulation + Performance roll (difficulty 2 if the target is the unit commander or another notable individual, 3 otherwise). For every two successes gained, the troops' Valor temporarily increases by a dot for the duration of the battle. A failed roll has no effect, but a botch may harm the resolve of the troops. The Courage-Building Address cannot be recast during a battle.

name: Glorious Battle Presence
summary: Capstone of the Compassion/social branch; lets a Lunar's battlefield commands carry clearly over a wide radius, grants bonus dice to leadership rolls, and immunizes his own troops to fear and intimidation effects.
description: Lunars are adept at combat, and they excel on the battlefield -- they are a fearsome sight and inspirational to an enemy and to their own allies. By means of this Charm, a Lunar can influence the performance of his troops in a battle. His commands are clearly audible to troops within (his Essence x 100) yards, and his player gains a bonus die equal to the character's Charisma when attempting any rolls involving leadership. Furthermore, any friendly troops within (the Lunar's Essence x 10) yards are immune to any effects that would reduce their Willpower or Valor and cannot fail Valor checks. Any enemy troops within the same radius are subject to an increase of 1 to the difficulty of resisting intimidation or demoralization.

name: Foe-Taunting Utterance
summary: Lets a Lunar deride an opponent's skill via a Manipulation + Presence roll, imposing stacking action and combat penalties on the target that scale with successes, resistible only by spending Willpower.
description: Insults are part of Lunar combat ritual -- deriding an opponent's reputation is almost as effective as a wound caused by a blade. However, most Lunars are inured to the taunts, ignoring them as part of the formalities. By means of this Charm, the Lunar gains insight into an opponent's skin and makes barbs that get under an opponent's skin and make her react. The Lunar's player makes a Manipulation + Presence roll against a difficulty equal to the opponent's Temperance. If the roll succeeds, the target is distracted and subtracts one success from all attacks, dodges and parries until the end of the next turn. Two or three successes indicate the comments have really gotten under the opponent's skin, penalizing the target's next initiative roll by 3. Five or more successes indicate the target goes wild -- she may not parry or dodge attacks, nor may she attack anyone other than the Lunar who taunted her for the remainder of the battle. However, the target is not subject to any initiative or attack roll penalties. This Charm may only be used on a single foe. The target may spend Willpower to offset its effects, each point allowing her to offset the taunt-induced penalties for the turn. The target must be within (the Lunar's Essence x 10) yards.

name: Glib Tongue Technique
summary: Lets a Lunar magically persuade a target to act (or not act) as he sees fit via a Manipulation + Presence roll against the target's permanent Essence, with success scaling from mere susceptibility to compulsion.
description: The Glib Tongue Technique builds on a Lunar's presence, allowing him to persuade an individual to act (or not act) as he sees fit. The Lunar's player rolls a Manipulation + Presence roll with a difficulty equal to the target's permanent Essence. The net successes determine whether the Lunar's manipulation succeeds or not: if the Lunar's player rolled one success, the subject is predisposed to the Exalt's suggestion and will likely do as the Lunar desires provided no influences (Charms, other persuasion attempts) come into play; three successes guarantee the subject's compliance with the suggestion, but she is still open to magical manipulations that convince her to do otherwise than what the Lunar says; five or more successes mean the subject will do as desired and cannot be swayed, and she will do so as soon as possible, even at great risk to herself.

name: Imposing Presence Attitude
summary: Lets a Lunar magnify his physical presence to intimidate, using Essence to appear larger or subtly terrifying and buying additional automatic dice for his Manipulation score on an intimidation attempt.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can overwhelm someone he is speaking to with his physical presence. Some use Essence to modify their size, making themselves appear larger, while others take on a more terrifying visage. A few are less obvious, subtly exuding menace and using barely controlled fury to scare the person they are facing. When the Lunar makes an intimidation attempt (see Exalted, p. 242), his player may purchase additional dice up to the Exalt's unmodified Manipulation score.

name: Fearful Lunar Form
summary: Lets a Lunar's battle-form guarantee a successful intimidation attempt against a group or an individual by converting dice up to his Manipulation into automatic successes.
description: The battle-form of a Lunar is a fearsome sight and more-or-less guarantees the success of an intimidation effort. When making an intimidation roll, the Lunar's player may convert a number of dice up to his character's Manipulation Attribute into automatic successes. Fearful Lunar Form is as effective against groups as it is against individuals; make one roll, and apply it to all who behold the Exalt's deadly glory.

name: Mind-Blanking Fear Technique
summary: Capstone of the Imposing Presence branch; lets a Lunar in beastman form induce short-term amnesia in a terrified target via Manipulation + Presence against the target's Essence.
description: A Lunar may focus his intimidation efforts on a single individual, seeking not only to force him into submission, but also to shatter his mind. If successful, the target's mind may be overwhelmed, perhaps rendering him unconscious or causing a derangement, but certainly damaging his short-term memory. The Lunar's player rolls Manipulation + Presence against a difficulty equal to the target's Essence. One success indicates that the target has forgotten what happened in the last minute, and each additional success increases this mind-blanking period by a minute. Mind-Blanking Fear Technique may only be targeted on an individual, and the Lunar employing it must be in beastman form.

name: Unspeaking Aura of Dread
summary: Root of the Interaction and Knowledge III tree; lets a Lunar spend Essence to add bonus dice to his Charisma for Social rolls against targets within range, even those who cannot understand his language.
description: Speech is only one method of manipulating others. Scent and body language can also play a part, particularly in more feral circumstances. A Lunar may attempt to use his protean nature to manipulate others by such nonverbal means, altering his posture, scent and a host of other factors to better influence others. When making a Social roll, the Lunar's player may purchase additional dice to his character's Charisma at a cost of 3 motes each. Such manipulation only works on targets within a number of yards equal to the Lunar's Essence, though the target need not understand his language (or even be able to hear him) to be affected.

name: Beast Calming Method
summary: Lets a Lunar soothe or pacify one or more animals via a Manipulation + Survival roll, with the required successes scaling by the beasts' disposition and ferocity.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can modify the mental state of a beast or a group of animals. This may be to pacify, or it may be to calm a skittish pachyderm he wants to calm. The difficulty of the Manipulation + Survival roll depends on the nature and number of the animals he seeks to influence. One success would allow the Lunar to walk past a rabbit without causing it to bolt, while three successes would hold a ravening pack of wolves in check. Five or more successes would cause even the mighty tyrant lizard to stand in abeyance. Animals need not understand the words of an Exalt seeking to calm them to be affected by the Charm.

name: Pack-Forming Presence
summary: Capstone of the Beast Calming Method branch; lets a Lunar command a following of beasts loyal for months at a time by accumulating successes on repeated Manipulation + Survival rolls over several days.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can seek to command beasts to do his bidding. To do so, his player must make a series of Manipulation + Survival rolls over a period of several days, during which time the Essence must remain committed. If the beasts are already friendly to the Lunar, he must accumulate one success for each beast he seeks to command, whereas, if they are neutral, three successes are needed for each. Hostile or fearful beasts cannot be easily commanded and must generally be convinced to give the Lunar a chance, usually by means of the Beast Calming Method. However, if the Lunar gets five successes with this Charm, even the most hostile beasts will acknowledge the Lunar as their pack-leader. Beasts commanded in this way remain loyal to the Lunar for a number of months equal to his Essence. After that time, he must either rework the Charm or trust to natural friendship. The Lunar may command a total number of beasts equal to (Charisma + Survival) x 10 via this Charm, though he may command more through natural loyalty. The cost of this Charm is paid per group of beasts (if social animals) or against individuals (if lone animals). If the Lunar spends 1 experience point when he enacts the Charm and uses it only on a single creature, he may spend an experience point to raise that beast's Familiar rating by 1. A character cannot get a new familiar unless his old one has died and cannot have more than one Familiar tied at a time. See the Solar Charm Spirit Tied Pet on page 179 of Exalted and the Familiar Background on page 143 for details.

name: Attention Demanding Presence
summary: Lets a Lunar silently draw the focused attention of everyone nearby via a Charisma + Presence roll, as though he had shouted 'look at me,' resistible with a point of temporary Willpower.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can focus the attention of those in the immediate vicinity upon himself without speaking. Doing so requires a Charisma + Presence roll; each success indicates that a number of individuals equal to the Exalt's Essence have received the Essence-driven equivalent of a shouted 'look at me.' These subjects find their attention focused on the Lunar and instinctively look into his eyes. A target may spend a point of temporary Willpower to resist the Charm's effect.

name: Animal Magnetism
summary: Capstone of the Attention Demanding Presence branch; lets a Lunar attempting seduction convert bonus dice up to his Essence, exploiting near-irresistible feral magnetism to determine the outcome.
description: A Lunar may use this Charm when seeking to seduce another character, exploiting his animal magnetism and feral nature with almost -- metaphorically -- deadly results; few can resist the focused attentions of a Lunar for long. When the Lunar makes the seduction attempt, his player may add bonus dice up to a number equal to the character's Essence. The number of successes determines the outcome of the seduction.

name: Brotherhood of Lake and River
summary: Root of the Interaction and Knowledge IV tree; forges a permanent blood-and-Essence sibling bond ('wolf-sibling') between a Lunar and another character, granting mutual awareness of direction, distance, and serious injury.
description: Though Lunars often live and act alone, they can form strong friendships and associations, similar to Solar Circles, they call 'packs.' That camaraderie is not the ultimate expression of a Lunar's loyalty; that ultimate expression is the Brotherhood of Lake and River, a bond of blood and Essence forged between the Lunar and his sibling-to-be brother. To partake in the Brotherhood of Lake and River, the Lunar and his sibling-to-be must cut the palm of their fellow's hand and bind the wounds together while the Charm is activated for at least 10 minutes. From that point on, the Lunar is always aware of his wolf-sibling's direction and distance and will know if the sibling sustains any serious injury -- or is killed. When in close proximity -- within 100 yards or so -- the Lunar may even read his wolf-sibling's surface thoughts. If the two have used the Charm reciprocally, they may even exchange words without being within 100 yards of one another. The effects are permanent and can only be broken by death. The maximum number of wolf-siblings a Lunar may have is equal to twice his Essence, though only one bond is formed with each use of the Charm. If such a packmate dies, another may take his place in the Lunar's heart. This Charm's effects are not automatically reciprocal; to establish a reciprocal link, two Lunars must use the Charm on one another.

name: Blood-Singing Instincts
summary: Lets a Lunar hunting with wolf-siblings present spend Essence to add to his initiative, tapping their blood ties and battlefield knowledge, with multiple linked Lunars able to share the same boosted initiative.
description: A Lunar hunting alone is a fearsome sight. Hunting with his associates is a nightmare for his enemies. She can exploit the blood and Essence ties to her allies, tapping into their senses and battlefield knowledge to gain a decisive edge. Before rolling initiative each turn, the Lunar may activate Blood-Singing Instincts, paying motes of Essence up to the number of allies present who are wolf-siblings of the Lunar through the Charm Brotherhood of Lake and River. Each mote of Essence spent in this manner adds 1 to the Lunar's player's initiative roll for the turn. Multiple Lunars can use one another to increase their initiative, making Lunars who hunt as a pack into the deadliest of foes.

name: Pack-Calling Cry
summary: Lets a Lunar summon any of his wolf-siblings from any distance via a magical call they feel compelled to obey, at a cost per sibling summoned, with resistance possible through Willpower.
description: By crying into the wind and sounding the Pack-Calling Cry, a Lunar uses the blood ties to his wolf-siblings in the Brotherhood of Lake and River to summon them into his presence. The Lunar may attempt to summon any number of those bound to him by the Brotherhood of Lake and River, each costing 1 mote of Essence. If summoning less than his full pack, the Lunar can select which of his packmates receive the summons. The call can be heard over any distance, implanting the desire to return to the Lunar's presence as soon as possible. The wolf-sibling has some leeway in deciding how quickly he heeds the call (a few minutes if nearby, perhaps hours if miles away, or thousands of days if hundreds or thousands of miles distant), but if he seeks to delay beyond this time, his player must make a Willpower roll against a difficulty equal to the calling Lunar's Charisma. Success allows the target to resist the call for the same time period again (which failure means he must break off what he is doing and set out toward the caller, though she may attempt to resist away for the same number of consecutive times equal to the calling Lunar's Essence.

name: Spirit-Scenting Technique
summary: Root of the Spirit Charms tree; lets a Lunar see spirits in his vicinity and undetectably discern a materialized spirit's true form, provided he does not use further Charms to aid the spirit.
description: By means of this Charm, a Lunar can 'see' spirits in his immediate vicinity, gaining an approximate idea of their forms and actions. Provided he is circumspect, and no Charms aid the spirit, this observation is undetectable. Furthermore, this Charm allows the Lunar to sense the true form of a materialized spirit -- a Lunar will know that a spirit masquerading as or possessing a human is not what it seems. The Charm does not allow the Lunar to communicate with or clearly comprehend the spirit. A Lunar who wishes to speak with gods, demons and elementals should learn Old Realm.

name: Pulse of the Invisible
summary: Lets a Lunar sense the flows and patterns of Essence around him, including the location and power of Manses and Demesnes, with a Perception + Occult roll revealing progressively deeper detail.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can adapt his senses to detect the flows and patterns of Essence in the world around him, as well as any dematerialized spirits present. The Exalt can instinctively sense the direction and strength of flows, as well as the locations and power of loci such as Manses and Demesnes. Ascertaining more detailed information requires a Perception + Occult roll. A single success grants the Lunar basic information about the examined location, such as identifying the nature of a sorcery or the general geomancy of a region, while additional successes provide more depth and specific detail. For example, three successes might allow the Lunar to judge the age and other specific details of the sorcery, while, with five successes, he might identify the sorcerer's 'signature' traits. Likewise, three successes provide the sort of detailed survey information necessary to construct a Manse, while five allow a near-perfect comprehension of an area's geomancy.

name: Devil-Restraining Grip
summary: Lets a Lunar bind a spirit within range via a Manipulation + Occult roll, preventing it from dematerializing and, if it lacks the Essence to remain manifest, forcing it to draw the deficit from the Lunar's own reserves.
description: Using the Devil-Restraining Grip Charm, a Lunar can immobilize a spirit with a snare of Essence, binding it to her as if on a leash. If the spirit is dematerialized, she can drive it into the material world, and once it is in physical form, it is prevented from dematerializing. To use this Charm, the Exalt's player makes a Manipulation + Occult roll against a difficulty equal to the spirit's Essence. If it succeeds, the spirit cannot move more than the Exalt has Essence Trait in yards and must materialize. If it does not have the Essence to materialize, then the additional Essence required is drained from the Lunar's reserves. If both the spirit and the Lunar cannot pay for the spirit's materialization, then the Essence is wasted, and the spirit remains immaterial.

name: Spirit-Maiming Essence Attack
summary: Capstone of the Spirit Charms tree; supplements a physical attack against a bound, hostile spirit to bolster its material-world efficacy, adding an Essence-based dice bonus to the aggravated damage caused.
description: If an encounter with a spirit goes wrong or the being is intrinsically hostile, then the Lunar may have to fight it, a difficult proposition against a possibly incorporeal foe. The Spirit-Maiming Essence Attack is one of the Lunar's most potent weapons in such a conflict, allowing him to use his strength of will to bolster his material attacks. The Lunar must activate this Charm before he attacks. If the attack is successful, the damage caused by the attack is aggravated, and, in addition, the Lunar's player reflexively rolls a number of dice equal to his Manipulation + Essence and adds a bonus equal to the number of successes to the base damage of the attack. Spirits destroyed with this Charm are gone forever, and the Lunar can sense those who know it and threaten them with the same wary respect reserved for those who can slay gods. Attacks enhanced with this Charm may explicitly be part of Combos with Charms of other Attributes.

name: Terrestrial Circle Sorcery
summary: Root sorcery-access Charm; enables a No Moon Lunar to learn and cast a single Terrestrial Circle spell, whose own Essence cost must be paid separately whenever it is cast; cannot be used in a Combo.
description: Terrestrial sorcery is the simplest magic wielded by Lunars, and the No Moons will initiate members of any caste as sorcerers provided an Exalt shows the appropriate intelligence and aptitude. Note that invoking this Charm only enables the character to cast a single Terrestrial Circle sorcery spell. The actual spell itself has an Essence cost, often very high, that the character must pay to actualize the spell; this cost is listed in the spell's description. Terrestrial Circle Sorcery can never be part of a Combo.

name: Form-Fixing Method
summary: Separate root of the Sorcery tree; lets a No Moon Lunar mystically fix a newly Exalted Lunar's caste and grant resistance to the Wyld's physical (not mental) warping, permanently spending experience points in the process.
description: Knowledge of this Charm allows a Lunar to tattoo a newly Exalted Lunar, fixing his caste and allowing him to resist the physical (but not mental) warping properties of the Wyld. The tattooing Lunar fixes the newly tattooed Exalt's caste as whichever he chooses; the tests of initiation are used only to determine the caste the tattooing Lunar assigns. This Charm is generally practiced only by Lunars of the No Moon Caste, though other Lunars may also know it; it is nonetheless considered inappropriate for Lunars of castes other than No Moon to tattoo young Lunars. Enacting this Charm requires a ceremony of several hours, during which occult instruments are used to draw the moonsilver tattoos into the Lunar's skin.

name: Tattoo-Cutting Wisdom
summary: Lets a Lunar engrave an item so that it becomes immune to Wyld warping effects, protecting it as though it were tattooed like a Lunar's own hide.
description: Using this Charm, a Lunar can engrave or otherwise mark an item so that it is immune to the chaotic effects of the Wyld, an untattooed Demesne or another source of shapechanging.

name: Moonsilver-Shaping Rite
summary: Lets a Lunar forge items from moonsilver, the only Exalt type with the spiritual connection to work the Magical Material effectively, at double the item's normal Essence cost, committed for the entire crafting process.
description: Though others may attempt to forge moonsilver, only a Lunar Exalted has the knowledge and spiritual connection to shape it effectively. Enacting this Charm forges a bond between the Lunar and the moonsilver being worked. Moonsilver is essentially impossible to work without the use of this Charm, and the technique is a jealously guarded secret of the Lunars. This bond must be maintained -- for the duration of the item-crafting effort, even when the object is not in the Lunar's immediate presence. Failing to maintain the Charm results in the immediate failure of the creation effort, though the moonsilver can be reused in a later project. The Essence cost of the Charm is twice the rating of the artifact the Lunar seeks to create; this is in addition to the basic Essence cost for creating the item (see Chapter Five of The Book of Three Circles for the specifics and rules of item creation).

name: Celestial Circle Sorcery
summary: Advanced sorcery-access Charm restricted to No Moon Lunars who undergo rigorous training; enables the caster to learn and cast a single Celestial Circle spell, whose own Essence cost must be paid separately; cannot be used in a Combo.
description: Celestial sorcery is much harder to learn and master than Terrestrial magics, and its practice among the No Moon Exalted is restricted to members of the No Moon Caste, who must undergo a rigorous (and often deadly) training regime before they are entrusted with its secrets. Note that invoking this Charm only enables the character to cast a single Celestial Circle sorcery spell. The actual spell itself has an Essence cost, often very high, that the character must pay to actualize the spell; this cost is listed in the spell's description. Celestial Circle Sorcery can never be part of a Combo.

name: Tentacles
summary: Splits one of the Lunars limb into multiple writhing tentacles, each capable of a separate attack against the same target.
description: The Lunar pours her Essence into one of her limbs, which splits into multiple, writhing tentacles. Anything held in that limb is dropped, but the Exalted natural attacks function as normal. Each of the tentacles is capable of making a separate attack at the Exalted full dice pool, although all must attack the same target. For each tentacle the Exalted wishes to create, she must spend 3 motes, and she cannot create more tendrils than her Essence. If the defender dodges, make one roll and apply it to all attacks.
cost: Varies (3 motes per tentacle, up to Essence in tentacles)

name: Summon Wild Beasts
summary: Calls Wyld-touched creatures native to the surrounding area to fight alongside the Lunar for a day.
description: The Exalted may summon creatures touched by the Wyld to him and direct them against his foe. The nature of the beast depends on the area where the summoning takes place. For example, in the Southwestern swamps, giant mutated toads may spring from the water to aid the Lunar. Each creature is around the size of a large dog, and the Exalted cannot summon more beasts than 10 times her Lore. See Exalted, p. 315, for creature statistics.
cost: 10 motes and 1 Willpower, +2 motes per creature

name: Acid Spit
summary: Transmutes the Lunars stomach acids into a corrosive phlegm that can be spat at a foe from range, dealing lingering damage until scraped off.
description: The Lunar channels Essence into his own digestive system, momentarily transforming the acids within his stomach into something far viler. He can then spit this corrosive phlegm onto his opponent. The phlegm has a range of 10 yards and does a damage of 4L + extra successes. It continues to do the basic damage each turn until it is scraped off its victim, which requires a successful Dexterity + Athletics roll. This roll is not a reflexive one and must be made as a separate action.

name: Mighty Thews
summary: Swells the Lunars muscles with Essence, temporarily boosting Strength through a Strength + Brawl roll.
description: When she uses Essence to enhance her very muscles via this Charm, a Lunar seems to swell into an intimidating, muscular version of herself. Tendons stand out like taught rope, and her muscles seem ready to burst through her skin. The Exalteds player makes a Strength + Brawl roll. For every success, add one to her Strength. The character cannot more than double her initial Strength through the use of this Charm. The Charms effect lasts for a number of turns equal to the characters Essence + the number of successes rolled.
cost: 2 motes per point of Strength gained

name: Strides of the Panther
summary: Reshapes the Lunars legs into a giant cats, doubling movement rate and tripling jumping distance for the scene.
description: The Lunars legs shift into the likeness of the legs of a giant cat, and his whole body twists slightly, becoming lower and more streamlined. For the remainder of the scene, the character can move at twice his normal movement rate and leap three times his normal jumping distance.
